name: Driver kind vs provider-instance split (open slugs)
what: A user can configure several instances of the same agent backend (for example a default Codex plus a personal and a work Codex); threads, sessions and runtime events always route by instance id, never by vendor kind.
how: Contracts split ProviderDriverKind (implementation selector, open branded slug /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/, max 64) from ProviderInstanceId (user-chosen routing slug). ServerSettings.providerInstances is a map instanceId -> {driver, displayName, accentColor, environment[], enabled, config:unknown}; driver-specific config stays opaque in the contract layer and each driver registers its own decoder. defaultInstanceIdForDriver(kind) returns the kind itself so legacy single-instance data stays routable. Unknown drivers must still parse and are surfaced as unavailable instead of crashing.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should key sessions on a routing instance id that is distinct from the vendor/driver kind, so one org can run several accounts, regions or keys of the same provider and still replay old threads. Baseline check: Verevon routes by inference-core intent (Budget/Balance/Genius) plus a privacy-tier floor and has a separate BYO ChatGPT subscription route; instance-scoped identity would unify those routes without replacing intent modes.
notes: Forward/backward-compat rule is explicit in the module doc: parsing must always succeed and the runtime marks unknown drivers unavailable (fork or rollback safety). Quality 5: Best-in-class: open slugs, forward/backward-compat rules and legacy promotion are explicit and tested by comments, beyond what peers expose.

name: Runtime provider snapshot streamed to the UI
what: The UI gets one live snapshot per configured provider instance: install/enabled state, auth identity (status, type, label, email), probe status (ready/warning/error/disabled), version, model list with per-model capabilities, slash commands, skills, update advisories and a human reason when a driver is unavailable.
how: ServerProvider schema in contracts/server.ts (instanceId, driver, displayName, accentColor, badgeLabel, continuation.groupKey, showInteractionModeToggle, requiresNewThreadForModelChange, enabled, installed, version, status, auth, checkedAt, availability, unavailableReason, models[], slashCommands[], skills[], versionAdvisory, updateState). Client projects it with deriveProviderInstanceEntries into ProviderInstanceEntry for pickers, settings and sidebar. Refresh cadence is settings.providerHealthRefreshInterval (default 5 minutes, RPC server.refreshProviders).
verevonRelevance: A single typed provider-health snapshot (auth identity + models + capabilities + advisories) feeding every picker is a clean contract for Verevon's model catalog and BYO-key status UI.
notes: Quality 4: Solid typed contract with auth, advisories and availability; the snapshot is rich but still CLI-centric.

name: Thread provider lock with continuation groups
what: Once a thread has started, the model picker only offers models from the same driver; switching to a different vendor mid-thread is blocked, while switching model (and between instances that share a continuation group) is allowed per turn.
how: deriveLockedProvider(thread) returns the session driver once threadHasStarted (latestTurn, messages or session exist). ChatComposer computes lockedContinuationGroupKey from the locked instance's snapshot.continuation.groupKey and filters compatible instances. ChatView.onProviderModelSelect rejects a different driver, rejects a different continuation group, and calls getStartedThreadModelChangeBlockReason which blocks any change when either provider sets requiresNewThreadForModelChange ('Start a new chat to change models'). ModelPickerContent greys out non-matching instances (lockedDisabledInstanceIds). Each turn carries its own modelSelection (ProviderSendTurnInput.modelSelection).
verevonRelevance: Verevon chat can allow free model switching per turn but needs an explicit rule for when provider-specific session state (resume cursors, tool schemas) makes a switch unsafe; the group-key idea gives that rule a data-driven form. Baseline check: Verevon resolves the model per turn server-side, so it has no lock today; the lock only matters if Verevon adds provider-bound sessions such as BYO subscription runs.
notes: Lock is by agent-harness continuity (CLI session resume), which is stricter than a plain chat product needs; Verevon's own harness could relax it by replaying normalized history. Quality 4: Correct and carefully guarded, but stricter than a non-CLI product needs; not mature as a general routing model.

name: Searchable multi-provider model picker with rail, favorites and legacy section
what: A popover with a left rail (Favorites plus one button per provider instance) and a virtualized model list; typing searches across all providers with fuzzy ranking; favorites float to the top; deprecated models sit in a collapsible 'Legacy models' group; models can be jumped to with Cmd/Ctrl+1..9.
how: ProviderModelPicker (Base UI Popover + ComposerControl trigger) renders ModelPickerContent: flatModels built from modelOptionsByInstance filtered by isProviderInstancePickerReady (enabled, available, status ready); tokenized scoring in modelPickerSearch.ts over name, shortName, subProvider, driverKind and instance display name with a +24 favorite boost; sorting via modelOrdering.sortProviderModelItems (favorites first, user modelOrder, then provider order); LegendList/ComboboxListVirtualized; favorites stored as {provider: instanceId, model} in client settings; keyboard jump commands modelPicker.jump.1..9 gated by when-context modelPickerOpen; global toggle modelPicker.toggle (mod+shift+m). Background scroll is locked while open.
verevonRelevance: Direct template for Verevon's model picker: instance rail, fuzzy tokenized search, favorites, legacy fold and number-key jumps are all small and cheap to port to SolidJS. Baseline check: Verevon's picker pins intent modes and groups the catalogue by vendor with expensive and privacy-tier badges; the baseline documents no fuzzy search, favorites, legacy fold or number-key jumps.
notes: Feels best-in-class for a power user with 5+ providers; no side-by-side comparison or cost/latency columns in the picker. Quality 5: Best picker seen: instance rail, tokenized fuzzy search, favorites, legacy fold, keyboard jumps and explanatory tooltips, all virtualized.

name: Capability-descriptor driven model traits (effort, thinking, fast mode, context window, agent)
what: Reasoning effort, thinking on/off, fast mode, context-window size and agent choice appear in the composer only when the selected model advertises them; the controls render generically from descriptors.
how: ModelCapabilities.optionDescriptors is a list of select|boolean descriptors (id, label, options[] with isDefault, currentValue, promptInjectedValues). TraitsPicker finds primary select, contextWindow, agent, fastMode and thinking descriptors via getProviderOptionDescriptors; selections are stored as ProviderOptionSelection[] {id,value} on ModelSelection.options (legacy object shape decoded by a transformOrFail migration; DB migration 026). Claude 'ultrathink' is a prompt-injected effort value: typing it applies a prefix and gives the composer frame an animated 'ultrathink-frame' style. Rendered as Menu radio groups; also exposed in a compact controls menu.
verevonRelevance: Server-declared option descriptors let Model Plane add new reasoning/tier knobs per model without frontend releases; the same descriptor list can carry cost tier or data-residency toggles.
notes: Quality 4: Clean descriptor-driven design that avoids per-model UI code; limited to select and boolean types.

name: Per-provider model aliasing, defaults and text-generation model
what: Short names like 'opus', 'sonnet', '5.4' resolve to canonical model ids per provider, each provider has a default model, and a cheaper default model is used for background text generation (titles, commit messages).
how: MODEL_SLUG_ALIASES_BY_PROVIDER, DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_PROVIDER and DEFAULT_TEXT_GENERATION_MODEL_BY_PROVIDER constants in contracts/model.ts (Codex gpt-5.6-sol default and gpt-5.6-luna for text; Claude claude-sonnet-5 and claude-haiku-4-5; Cursor auto/composer-2; Grok grok-build; OpenCode openai/gpt-5). Separate settings textGenerationModelSelection and sourceControlWriterModelSelection let the user pin these.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should separate a 'chat model' from a cheap 'utility model' (titles, summaries, query rewriting) with its own routing and cost line.
notes: Model names are code constants in this build, not a live registry. Quality 4: Practical and complete for five drivers, but model ids are hard-coded constants.

name: Multi-account provider instances via home-path isolation
what: Two logins of the same CLI agent (work and personal Claude or Codex) can coexist as separate provider instances, each with its own binary path, config home, launch args and environment variables.
how: CodexSettings fields binaryPath, homePath (CODEX_HOME), shadowHomePath ('account-specific Codex home that keeps auth.json separate while sharing state'), launchArgs; ClaudeSettings binaryPath, homePath (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), autoCompactWindow, launchArgs. Instance envelope also carries environment[] (name, value, sensitive, valueRedacted). Server drivers: ClaudeHome, CodexHomeLayout, ClaudeExecutable.
verevonRelevance: Account isolation by config-home is CLI-specific, but the product idea (several credentialed identities per provider, selectable per thread) applies to Verevon's org/personal key separation.
notes: server files cited by name from scout inventory; settings.ts lines verified. Quality 4: Works through CLI home isolation; CLI-specific and not a general credential model.

name: Schema-annotated provider settings forms
what: Each provider's settings screen (binary path, home, launch args, auto-compact window) is generated from its schema, so adding a field or a driver needs no bespoke form code.
how: makeProviderSettingsSchema(fields, {order}) adds Effect Schema annotations providerSettingsForm {control: text|password|textarea|switch, placeholder, hidden, clearWhenEmpty} and providerSettingsFormSchema {order}. ProviderSettingsForm.deriveProviderSettingsFields reads annotations, sorts by order, titleizes keys and renders Input/Switch/Textarea; unknown drivers fall back to a read-only card so envelopes round-trip. PROVIDER_CLIENT_DEFINITIONS lists label, icon, settingsSchema and an optional 'Early Access' badge.
verevonRelevance: Schema-driven settings pages are a good fit for Verevon's typed Rust contracts (serde + JSON Schema annotations -> generated Solid forms).
notes: Quality 4: Compact and extensible; annotations cover only four control types.

name: Add-provider wizard and 'coming soon' driver roster
what: Settings > Providers offers a three-step wizard (Driver, Identity, Config) that validates the instance id before proceeding; GitHub Copilot, Gemini, ACP Registry and Pi Agent are shown as coming soon.
how: AddProviderInstanceDialog with ADD_PROVIDER_WIZARD_STEPS and resolveWizardNavigation (forward navigation past Identity blocked until instance id passes validateInstanceId: slug rules, <=64 chars, unique); instance id is derived as <driver>_<slugified label>; accent colour swatches (#2563eb, #16a34a, ...) and normalizeProviderAccentColor (#rrggbb only); COMING_SOON_DRIVER_OPTIONS array.
verevonRelevance: Shows the roadmap direction (Gemini and an ACP registry) and a small, validated wizard pattern for adding provider connections.
notes: Quality 4: Small validated wizard; functional rather than distinctive.

name: Provider accent colour and account badge on icons
what: Each instance can have an accent colour, and its icon gets a small badge whenever several instances share a driver, so 'Codex (work)' and 'Codex (personal)' are never confused in the composer, picker rail or sidebar.
how: shouldShowInstanceBadge(entry, entries) true when accentColor set or the driver appears more than once; ProviderInstanceIcon renders the badge; ProviderAccentColorPicker in settings; resolveInstanceDisplayName falls back to a humanized instance id (codex_personal -> Codex Personal).
verevonRelevance: Cheap but effective multi-identity affordance for Verevon when a user switches between org-managed and personal model access.
notes: Quality 4: Simple, effective disambiguation of same-driver instances.

name: Provider update advisories and one-click CLI updates
what: The app checks whether each provider CLI is behind its latest version and shows launch/primary notifications and a sidebar pill; the user can trigger an update with progress output.
how: ServerProviderVersionAdvisory {status unknown|current|behind_latest, currentVersion, latestVersion, updateCommand, canUpdate, checkedAt, message} and ServerProviderUpdateState {idle|queued|running|succeeded|failed|unchanged, output<=10k chars}; setting enableProviderUpdateChecks; dismissedProviderUpdateNotificationKeys; ProviderUpdateLaunchNotification, ProviderUpdatePrimaryNotification, SidebarProviderUpdatePill; RPC server.updateProvider with installer kinds brew, bun, npm, pnpm and variants (per scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Mostly CLI-specific; relevant analog is surfacing model deprecations and version advisories for hosted models in Verevon's model catalog.
notes: Quality 4: Well built for CLIs; the update mechanics are installer-specific.

name: Virtualized timeline with strict live-follow and message anchoring
what: Long threads stay smooth because rows are virtualized; the view follows the streaming edge only while the user is at the bottom, a 'Scroll to end' pill appears when they drift, and a sent message can be anchored near the top.
how: MessagesTimeline owns a @legendapp/list LegendList (patched build) with maintainScrollAtEnd {animated:false,on:{dataChange,itemLayout,layout}}; liveFollowEnabled prop gates re-pinning; TIMELINE_FOLLOW_REARM_THRESHOLD_PX = 40 (comment explains LegendList isNearEnd is too loose and yanked readers down); anchorMessageId + onAnchorReady; contentInsetEndAdjustment = composer overlay height so the composer floats over the list; disclosure toggles suspend end-pinning for two animation frames (disclosureToggleSettling) so expanding a fold does not jump; useStableRows structurally shares unchanged row objects. Older turns load via a 'Load earlier' header row.
verevonRelevance: Streaming chat quality depends on exactly these details (follow re-arm band, anchor-on-send, overlay composer inset); Verevon's Solid timeline should adopt a virtual list plus an explicit follow state machine rather than naive scrollIntoView. Baseline check: Verevon chat has no list virtualization and reparses the whole message on every streamed token (baseline known gap 14), so this timeline design is a direct remedy.
notes: Comments in the source record real regressions (reader yanked down on stream chunk), which makes the rules trustworthy. Quality 5: Excellent: strict follow band, anchoring, overlay inset and disclosure settling each fix a documented regression.

name: Settled-turn folding behind a 'Worked for ...' row
what: After a turn finishes, the noisy middle (tool calls, intermediate commentary) collapses behind a single 'Worked for 2m 14s' toggle while the first and final assistant messages stay visible; running turns never fold.
how: deriveTurnFolds() groups entries per turn, keeps first and terminal assistant messages, and emits a 'turn-fold' row anchored at the first hidden entry; unsettled turn is derived from session running turn then latestTurn lifecycle (not transient working state) so folding does not flicker when a message is sent; startBoundary uses the triggering user message time for the duration label; expandedTurnIds state in MessagesTimeline; TurnFoldTimelineRow renders an aria-expanded button.
verevonRelevance: Agent pages that run many tool calls need a default-collapsed work history with a duration label; this is the cleanest pattern seen in this audit for keeping answers prominent while keeping the trace one click away. Baseline check: Verevon keeps trace in a Work/Output/Sources/Trace canvas; an in-thread 'Worked for' fold is a complementary default that keeps the answer prominent.
notes: Quality 5: Best-in-class default: keeps first and final answers visible, derives unsettled state from lifecycle to avoid flicker.

name: Tool-call work log with grouping, live row and expandable detail
what: Each tool call, command, subagent spawn, hook and thinking step is shown as a compact row with icon, label, status and expandable raw command/output; consecutive tool calls collapse into a group summarized like 'Read 4 files, ran 2 commands'.
how: session-logic.deriveWorkLogEntries builds WorkLogEntry {toolCallId, label, detail, command, rawCommand, changedFiles, tone thinking|tool|info|error, toolLifecycleStatus inProgress|completed|failed|declined|stopped, taskId, agentRole, agentSpawn}; MessagesTimeline.logic derives row kinds work, work-live, work-toggle (hiddenCount, summary, summaryKind, hasFailure); MAX_VISIBLE_WORK_LOG_ENTRIES=1 so only the latest row is visible until expanded; summarizeToolGroup is the provider-neutral fallback; omitSupersededLifecycleMarkers collapses in-progress rows into their completed twins; a shell tokenizer (tokenizeShellCommand, commandProgramName, command wrappers) turns raw commands into friendly names; failure rows highlighted via workEntryIndicatesToolFailure.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon's agent pages a ready-made information architecture for transparency: one-line live status, grouped summaries, per-call raw detail, failure emphasis. Baseline check: Verevon already has tool cards with intent icons, a Work panel and a Trace tab; adopt T3's grouping summaries, superseded-lifecycle collapsing and shell-command labelling rather than replacing them.
notes: Summaries are rule-based; no LLM-generated summary was found (comment mentions 'generated tool summaries' as a disabled/unavailable path). Quality 5: Very mature grouping, live row and command labelling; summaries are rule-based rather than generated.

name: Left-edge timeline minimap with hover previews
what: A slim rail along the left of the chat shows one tick per user message; hovering shows a card with the user's prompt and the turn's final answer, and clicking jumps there.
how: deriveTimelineMinimapItems collects user rows with compactMinimapPreview of user text and resolveFinalAssistantTextForTurn; TimelineMinimap positions ticks by index (resolveTimelineMinimapTopPercent), uses a hit strip whose width is capped to the gutter so it never covers message text (resolveTimelineMinimapHitStripWidth), a persistent gutter on wide viewports (TIMELINE_MINIMAP_PERSISTENT_GUTTER=48), min 2 items, max height calc(100vh - 18rem), content column max width 768px; keeps preview interactive while open.
verevonRelevance: A low-cost navigation aid for long research/agent conversations that none of the reference chat apps in this audit expose; fits Verevon's long-running agent threads.
notes: Quality 4: Polished and gutter-aware; niche but well executed.

name: Rich markdown rendering with table and code-block chrome
what: Assistant text renders GFM, GitHub-style alert blockquotes, task lists, collapsible details, tables with expand-cells and copy as Markdown or CSV, and code blocks with filename title, language icon, wrap toggle and copy.
how: ChatMarkdown composes react-markdown with remark-gfm, remark-breaks, rehype-raw and rehype-sanitize (custom schema keeps Windows drive image paths via rehypeNormalizeWindowsImageSrc), remarkGithubAlerts (five alert kinds with glyph and colour), remarkPreserveCodeMeta (fence meta like title=), MarkdownTable (serializeTableElementToMarkdown/Csv), MarkdownDetails, MarkdownCodeBlock (header with title, wrap, copy; data-language and data-wrap attributes). Shiki highlighting is suspense-based with a size-aware LRU cache keyed by fnv1a hash of code+language+theme and the cache is bypassed while streaming. Word-wrap default comes from client setting wordWrap.
verevonRelevance: Baseline markdown parity; table-to-CSV copy and streaming-aware highlight caching are the cheap wins. Math, Mermaid and chart rendering are absent and remain a gap Verevon can exploit. Baseline check: Verevon already renders KaTeX, Mermaid, accessible SVG charts and citations with its own parser; T3 only adds table copy-as-CSV chrome and the streaming-aware highlight cache.
notes: No KaTeX/Mermaid/citations in this build (scout and my grep agree). Quality 4: Good but standard: no math, Mermaid or citations; chrome and caching are well done.

name: File paths in answers become actionable chips; workspace images load via signed URLs
what: File references in assistant text render as file chips with icons; clicking opens the file in the in-app panel at the referenced line, or in the preferred editor, browser, or reveals it in the OS file manager; markdown images that point at workspace files load through signed asset URLs.
how: remarkNormalizeLinksAndTagInlineCode tags inline code that looks like a path; MarkdownFileLink (props targetPath, workspaceRelativePath, line, onOpenInPanel, openInEditorMenuLabel, onReveal with platform label) with context menu; buildFileLinkParentSuffixByPath disambiguates identical basenames with parent folder suffix; useOpenInPreferredEditor / usePreferredEditor (editorPreferences) with editor targets; ChatMarkdownWorkspaceImage resolves classifyMarkdownImageSource and fetches via RPC assets.createUrl.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon, the equivalent is making document, record and source references in answers first-class chips that open the right Data-plane object in a side panel.
notes: Quality 4: Strong workspace integration with disambiguation and signed image URLs; coding-centric.

name: Message affordances: collapsed long prompts, hover actions, day-aware timestamps
what: Very long user messages collapse to 8 lines/600 characters with a fade mask and a toggle; copy and timestamp controls on assistant messages appear on hover/focus; timestamps are day-aware with a full tooltip.
how: CollapsibleUserMessageBody with MAX_COLLAPSED_USER_MESSAGE_LINES=8, MAX_COLLAPSED_USER_MESSAGE_LENGTH=600, a linear-gradient mask; assistant meta row uses opacity-0 group-hover/assistant:opacity-100 and focus-within so keyboard users still reach it; formatDayAwareTimestamp and formatChatTimestampTooltip honour timestampFormat (locale, 12-hour, 24-hour); RevertUserMessageButton for checkpoint revert at a user message; skill mentions rendered inline in user text; terminal/element/annotation/review-comment contexts rendered as chips.
verevonRelevance: Small polish items worth copying: prompt collapse, keyboard-reachable hover actions, tabular-nums timestamps.
notes: No edit-and-resend, regenerate or branch buttons exist in this UI (scout confirmed; only revert-to-checkpoint). Quality 4: Competent polish; lacks edit, regenerate and branch actions found in peers.

name: Draft 'hero' composer: centered prompt with inline project switcher
what: A new thread opens as a calm centered composer with a headline like 'What should we work on in <project>' where the project name is a dotted-underline dropdown; sending animates the composer down to the docked position.
how: ChatView computes isDraftHeroState and renders the composer overlay inset-0 centered (otherwise absolute bottom-0); DraftHeroHeadline builds picker entries from sidebarProjectGrouping and calls handleNewThread(..., {replace:true, carryComposerContent:true}) so typed text survives a project change; useDraftHeroLayoutTransition animates layout (DRAFT_HERO_TRANSITION_DURATION_MS=180, cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)) and skips under prefers-reduced-motion; on phones runMobileComposerTransition uses the View Transitions API with named transitions (t3-mobile-composer, t3-mobile-draft-headline); the index route auto-creates a draft in the most recently active project so the first screen is always a prompt.
verevonRelevance: First-screen design Verevon can mirror: land straight in a prompt, scope chosen inline in the headline, no dead-end empty state.
notes: Also shows a graceful reduced-motion path. Quality 4: Smooth and thoughtful with reduced-motion handling; a common pattern executed well.

name: Inbox-style thread sidebar with pinned, snoozed and settled lifecycle
what: The left sidebar is a working inbox: pinned threads (drag to reorder), active threads, snoozed threads that wake later, and a collapsed 'Settled (N)' tail; thread rows show status pills and elapsed working time, and a 'Woke' notice appears when a snooze ends or the agent raises its hand.
how: Sidebar.tsx (3960 lines) with dnd-kit sortable pinned rows (SortablePinnedThreadRow), search box (searchSidebarThreadsByTitle), project filter menu ('All projects'), New thread/New project buttons, thread jump hints (Cmd+1..9 with 200ms delayed hint badges), multi-select with bulk archive and bulk title regeneration; useThreadActions exposes settle/unsettle/snooze/unsnooze/pin/unpin/reorderPinned/archive/delete; client-runtime/state/threadSettled and threadSort hold the pure lifecycle logic shared with the mobile app; sidebar width is resizable (min width, clamp to leave main content min width) and persisted.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agents run long and in parallel; an attention-ordered inbox (needs approval > needs input > working > plan ready > unseen completion) beats a flat chat history for the agent pages. Baseline check: Verevon's thread list is capped at 80 without paging, projects are a browser-only organizer and the Fleet console is a stub, so an attention-ordered inbox is a clear upgrade for agent runs.
notes: A legacy per-project tree sidebar still ships behind legacySidebarEnabled (LegacySidebar.tsx, 138KB). Quality 5: Best-in-class for agent workloads: attention ordering, pins, snooze, settle and woke states in one coherent list.

name: Thread status pills with attention-priority rollup and unseen-completion tracking
what: Every thread shows one status (Pending Approval, Awaiting Input, Working, Connecting, Plan Ready, Monitoring, Completed) and project rows roll up the highest-priority child status; completion only shows for threads the user has not visited since.
how: resolveThreadStatusPill() applies a fixed precedence (approval, user input, running, starting, plan-ready, background liveness working/monitoring, unseen completion); THREAD_STATUS_PRIORITY ranks labels 6..1 for resolveProjectStatusIndicator; hasUnseenCompletion compares latestTurn.completedAt with lastVisitedAt; backgroundLiveness (working|monitoring) keeps sidebar status live after the turn ends when subagents or monitors still run; each pill has colour classes and a pulse flag; failed sessions outrank stale background liveness.
verevonRelevance: Direct blueprint for Verevon's agent run list: a small closed set of attention states with deterministic precedence is what keeps parallel agents manageable. Baseline check: Verevon's agent pages are mostly blueprints; a closed, ranked status vocabulary would anchor the real run list once runs are wired.
notes: Quality 5: Best-in-class: closed vocabulary, deterministic precedence, unseen-completion tracking, unit-testable pure functions.

name: Settle and snooze lifecycle with client/server twin invariants
what: A thread can be settled (done) manually, automatically after N days of inactivity, or when its pull request merges or closes; or snoozed until an hour, evening, tomorrow or next week; blocked threads (waiting on approval or input) cannot be hidden, and a snoozed thread wakes early if the agent needs the user.
how: threadSettled.ts: effectiveSettled (activity blockers first, then explicit settledOverride, then PR merged/closed via changeRequestAutoSettles, then inactivity window; open PR blocks inactivity), canSettle/canSnooze (client twins of server invariants), threadRaisedHandWhileSnoozed, threadWokeAt (drives the Woke indicator), resolveSnoozePresets (hour, three-hours, evening, tomorrow, next-week), snoozeWakeLabel ('2h','3d'); hasQueuedTurnStart with a 2-minute grace; client settings sidebarAutoSettleAfterDays (default 3) and sidebarAutoSettleOnMerge (default true); commands thread.settle/unsettle/snooze/unsnooze; keybinding thread.settle (mod+shift+s).
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a principled 'done/snoozed/needs-me' model for long-running agents, including event-based wake and tying completion to external state (PR merged) rather than only time. Baseline check: Verevon has run watchers ('Notify me when done') but no settle/snooze states or event-based wake; this could sit on top of the existing watchers.
notes: Snooze wake is derived client-side from timestamps; no server event fires when it expires. Quality 5: Best-in-class: server and client twin invariants, event-based wake and PR-aware auto-settle.

name: Three-surface global search overlay with one reducer (commands, files, content)
what: Cmd/Ctrl+K opens a palette to search commands, projects and threads (including message content snippets); Cmd+P jumps to a file; Cmd+Shift+F searches project contents; re-pressing a shortcut toggles it closed and the three modes never stack.
how: CommandPalette.logic.reduceCommandPaletteUiState over SearchOverlayMode command|files|content; CommandPaletteItem {kind action|submenu, searchTerms, threadContentMatch{source user|assistant,snippet}, shortcutCommand}; modes root, root-browse (type a path to add a project), submenu, submenu-browse; items include New thread, New thread in..., Go to file, Search project contents, Add project (local folder, clone repository, WSL folder, remote sources), Open settings, Project settings, Toggle theme editor; thread-content hits come from RPC orchestration.searchThreads; the first 9 thread entries receive thread.jump.N shortcut hints; commandPaletteBus opens it from anywhere via a window CustomEvent.
verevonRelevance: One keyboard-first entry for navigation, actions and conversation search is a baseline Verevon should ship; the mutually exclusive overlay reducer is a good small design. Baseline check: Verevon has no command palette or shortcut sheet (planned I1) and only opens global search with Ctrl/Cmd+K or '/'.
notes: Quality 4: Well-factored overlay reducer; the search itself is literal matching.

name: Themeable design tokens with light/dark halves, OKLCH palette engine and live editor
what: Five built-in themes (T3 Chat, Grove, Ocean, Ember, Iris), custom themes, separate light and dark theme choices (mix and match), a guided editor that generates a contrast-solved palette from a canvas and accent colour, VS Code theme import and Open VSX search/install; the editor paints the live app and includes an element inspector that shows which colour role paints what.
how: packages/shared/themePalettes.ts defines ~56 product colour roles (canvas, chrome, toolbar*, surface*, text, border, focus, accent*, message*, code*, sidebar*, terminal*) shared by web CSS and React Native; themePalette.ts (1976 lines) holds ThemeFile v1, localStorage keys (t3code:themes:v1, theme-follow-system, theme-appearance-mode, theme-halves:v1), OKLCH conversion, gamut mapping (greatest sRGB-fitting chroma), binary-search lightness to hit contrast targets; useTheme syncs the Electron nativeTheme (desktop:set-theme) and meta theme-color; ThemeEditorHost mounts above the router (themeEditorStore) so a draft survives navigation; themeInspector probes tokens with sentinel colours (#01fea7/#fe01a7) and draws an SVG spotlight; vscodeThemeImport derives a full palette from the editor background and accent then overlays specified workbench keys; openVsxThemes reads VSIX via jszip. Tailwind v4.3 CSS custom properties (--background, --primary, --sidebar-*, --glass-*) are the runtime surface.
verevonRelevance: Verevon could ship a role-token theme system (also reusable for tenant branding) with a contrast-solving generator; the live inspector is a differentiating customization UX. Baseline check: the baseline lists only a theme saved via the navbar action; a role-token palette with a contrast solver would also serve tenant branding.
notes: Theming reaches terminal colours and sidebar artwork too. Built CSS confirms Tailwind v4.3.0 with oklch custom properties (index-DSuALXPn.css). Quality 5: Best-in-class customization: role tokens, contrast-solved generation, VS Code import and a live inspector.

name: Granular appearance controls (fonts, sizes, contrast, glass, smoothing)
what: Users tune four independent font families (code, composer, sans, terminal) and sizes, an appearance contrast slider (50-200), glass/translucency opacity (40-100), grayscale font smoothing, word wrap and timestamp format.
how: ClientSettingsSchema fields fontFamilyCode/Composer/Sans/Terminal, fontSizeInterface (12-20, default 16), fontSizePrompt (12-20, 14), fontSizeCode (10-18, 13), fontSizeTerminal (8-20, 12), appearanceContrast (50-200), glassOpacity (40-100, default 80), fontSmoothing, wordWrap, timestampFormat; appearanceFonts.ts (14.7KB) resolves stacks; FontFamilyPicker and SettingsFontPreviews render live previews; CSS tokens --glass-blur:12px, --glass-opacity, --glass-saturation:1.14.
verevonRelevance: A compact, bounded set of density/typography knobs (each with min/max/default constants) is a good settings pattern; Verevon needs an equivalent for accessibility and per-tenant branding.
notes: Quality 4: Bounded, well-defaulted controls; breadth is good, not unique.

name: Build-stage identification via sidebar artwork or pill
what: The sidebar header can show stage artwork (for example nightly or dev builds) or a text pill so people running several environments or channels never confuse them.
how: environmentIdentificationMode artwork|pill|none (default artwork); SidebarStageBackdrop with --stage-art-* and --stage-night-* OKLCH tokens, resolveSidebarStageBackdropVariant and resolveEnvironmentIdentificationPillLabel; useEnvironmentStageLabel; theme definitions can opt in with sidebarArtwork.
verevonRelevance: Useful for Verevon when users juggle prod, staging and sandbox tenants or regions (visual cue that cannot be missed).
notes: Quality 3: Neat but narrow purpose.

name: Lexical composer with inline tokens (files, skills, terminal output)
what: The prompt box is a rich-text editor where @file mentions, $skill references and pasted terminal selections appear as atomic inline chips that behave like single characters for cursor, backspace and selection, while the underlying prompt stays plain text.
how: ComposerPromptEditor (Lexical 0.41) defines DecoratorNodes ComposerMentionNode, ComposerSkillNode, ComposerTerminalContextNode with plugins for arrow navigation across tokens, Home/End, backspace, selection normalisation, chip selection, token paste and surround-selection; text-length arithmetic maps between 'collapsed' (one char per chip) and 'expanded' (serialized path) offsets; composerTrigger.detectComposerTrigger recognises @path, /command and $skill at the cursor; serializeComposerFileLink emits markdown links; drag a file from the tree to insert a mention (composerMentionDrag, workspaceFileDrop).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's composer needs the same inline chips for Data-plane documents, people, tools and skills; the collapsed/expanded offset model is the hard part and is worth studying.
notes: Heavy implementation (editor file is 56KB); Solid has no direct Lexical equivalent, so budget real engineering. Quality 4: Very capable but heavy and intricate; high maintenance cost.

name: Slash commands, skills menu and keyboard-first send semantics
what: Typing '/' opens a command menu (including /model, /plan, /default and provider slash commands) and '$' lists provider skills; Enter sends, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter on a new draft starts the thread in the background without switching to it.
how: ComposerCommandMenu with composerSlashCommandSearch and providerSkillSearch; built-in items are /model (clears the trigger text and opens the model picker through setIsComposerModelPickerOpen), and /plan and /default only when planModeEnabled; the active provider instance's slashCommands appear as /<name> and its skills as /skill:<name>, so the menu differs per selected provider (ChatComposer.tsx around lines 1137-1200 and 1815-1835); ServerProvider.slashCommands[] (name, description, input.hint) and skills[] (name, path, scope, enabled, displayName, shortDescription) come from the provider snapshot; ComposerTriggerKind path|slash-command|slash-model|skill; composerSubmissionIntentForEnter returns null on mobile or with Shift, 'background' for modifier+Enter on a draft, otherwise 'foreground'; ChatView threads submissionIntent through beginLocalDispatch and beginBackgroundDraftSubmissionByRef so the hero composer only docks for foreground sends; setting showSkillsInSlashMenu (default true).
verevonRelevance: Background-start (fire an agent and stay where you are) is a good fit for Verevon agent pages that launch many parallel runs.
notes: Quality 4: Solid; provider-specific menus and background-start are good touches.

name: Four runtime modes selectable per thread in the composer footer
what: A footer dropdown sets how much the agent may do without asking: Supervised (ask before commands and file changes), Auto-accept edits, Auto (supported providers approve routine actions, others still ask) and Full access; an adjacent Plan/Build toggle appears for providers that support it.
how: runtimeModeConfig in ChatComposer maps RuntimeMode approval-required|auto-accept-edits|auto|full-access to label, description and lucide icon; ComposerFooterModeControls renders a Base UI Select with two-line items; handleRuntimeModeChange persists via thread.runtime-mode.set; interaction mode default|plan via thread.interaction-mode.set, shown only when ServerProvider.showInteractionModeToggle is true; runtime mode travels on thread creation and every turn.start; server maps to provider-native modes (Claude bypassPermissions/acceptEdits, Codex read-only/workspace-write/danger-full-access per scout).
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same four-step autonomy ladder, but governed by org policy (an admin ceiling per space) rather than purely user choice. Baseline check: Verevon's Ask/Do switch and autonomy rungs (read_only, workspace_write, danger_full_access, with a written justification) already cover this more strictly; T3 adds an in-between 'auto-accept edits' step.
notes: Correction to scout inventory: a fourth mode 'auto' exists in the UI; the scout listed three. Quality 4: Clear and well-described, but default is the most permissive mode.

name: Inline approval and structured-question cards docked to the composer
what: When the agent needs permission, the composer footer turns into an approval strip showing the exact command, file or app request with Cancel, Decline, 'Always allow this session' and Approve; agent questions appear as a stepper card with options and a free-text answer.
how: ComposerPendingApprovalPanel renders requestKind-specific labels (command, file-read, file change, mcp-elicitation 'App access approval'), a focusable scrollable <code> block with data-approval-detail and an N/M counter; ComposerPendingApprovalActions defaults [cancel, decline, acceptForSession, accept] but uses provider-supplied options when present (ProviderApprovalOption); ComposerPendingUserInputPanel keeps per-question draft answers, multiSelect, optimistic single-select with auto-advance timer, collapsible header so a tall prompt does not cover the thread, and sending from the composer advances the question; derivePendingApprovals and derivePendingUserInputs read orchestration activities (approval.requested/resolved, user-input.requested/resolved).
verevonRelevance: Approvals that sit next to the input (not in a modal) with the full command visible and a session-scoped 'always allow' are the right pattern for Verevon computer-use and connector actions. Baseline check: Verevon already has approval cards, an editable plan gate and authority rungs; take only the composer-docked placement and the 'always allow this session' option, subject to org policy.
notes: Approval options come from the provider, so granularity of 'always allow' is provider-defined. Quality 4: Excellent placement and detail visibility; 'always allow' granularity depends on the provider.

name: Plan mode with proposed-plan card, follow-up banner and 'implement in new thread'
what: In plan mode the agent returns a proposed plan shown as a collapsible card that can be copied, downloaded or saved into the workspace; a 'Plan ready' banner offers to implement it, optionally in a fresh thread; a segmented progress bar tracks task steps during execution.
how: Orchestration events turn.proposed.delta/completed and thread.proposed-plan.upsert (ProposedPlan with implementedAt and implementationThreadId); ProposedPlanCard (collapsed preview markdown, export filename builder, writeProjectFile to save into workspace), ComposerPlanFollowUpBanner, onImplementPlanInNewThread; ComposerTasksBadge renders TaskSegments (3px segments completed=success, inProgress=primary, pending=muted) from turn.plan.updated steps with durations; plan-mode toggle is now behind client setting planModeEnabled (legacy beta) because the Build/Plan toggle was removed from the default UI.
verevonRelevance: Plan-then-implement with a persisted plan object and an explicit hand-off to a new run is useful for Verevon workflows where a reviewed plan gates tool execution.
notes: Plan toggle demoted to a beta flag suggests the team found always-visible Plan/Build confusing. Quality 4: Complete flow, but the toggle was demoted to a legacy beta flag.

name: Context-window ring with manual compaction and stale-session compaction offer
what: A small ring in the composer shows context usage (turns red above 90%); hovering reveals used/max tokens, total processed and a 'Compact context' button, and when a long Claude session has been idle for 70+ minutes with 100k+ tokens the agent asks whether to compact before continuing.
how: ContextWindowMeter (SVG circle with dashoffset animation honoring motion-reduce) reads ContextWindowSnapshot (usedTokens, maxTokens, usedPercentage, totalProcessedTokens, compactsAutomatically, autoCompactThreshold) built from thread.token-usage.updated events; onCompact is ChatComposer.compactThreadContext, which refuses while a run, approval, pending input or image compression is in flight and otherwise injects the provider-native '/compact' slash command as an ordinary prompt through submitComposer (then clears it if dispatch was blocked); shouldOfferResumeCompaction uses CLAUDE_RESUME_COMPACTION_MINUTES=70 and CLAUDE_RESUME_COMPACTION_TOKENS=100000; the server adapter asks a user-input question whose text and 'Don't ask again' answer live in packages/shared/claudeCompaction.ts so client and server agree; dismissal persisted via t3code:resume-compaction-dismissed and resolved user-input activity; Claude setting autoCompactWindow (100k-1M).
verevonRelevance: Verevon should expose context usage and an explicit compact action, and could add a cost-aware 'resume' prompt for stale long sessions. Baseline check: Verevon has MG compaction and a context inspector but no live spend meter; a ring plus Compact button is a compact entry point to both.
notes: The 70-minute threshold likely tracks prompt-cache expiry (INF low; basis: constant name and the cost framing, no comment states it). Manual compaction is only enabled when the selected provider is claudeAgent (ChatView compactDisabled), with specific reasons such as 'Send or clear your draft before compacting'; other providers only show the passive ring. Quality 4: Useful and honest; manual compaction is Claude-only and the cache-TTL rationale is inferred.

name: Image attachments with background upload queue, HEIC conversion and compression
what: Images can be pasted, dropped or picked; they upload in the background (3 at a time per environment), HEIC/HEIF photos are converted in the browser, and oversized images are shrunk to fit the 10 MB wire cap; up to 8 images per turn.
how: attachmentUploadQueue (MAX_UPLOADS_PER_ENVIRONMENT=3, UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS=5 min, zustand store of AttachmentUploadState per image id) posts to /api/attachments/upload; imageCompression.ts (MAX_DIMENSION 2048, 50 MB source cap, HEIC decode pixel cap 64M, iterative dimension/quality stepping, heic-to lazy chunk); contracts PROVIDER_SEND_TURN_MAX_ATTACHMENTS=8, MAX_IMAGE_BYTES=10 MB, MAX_INPUT_CHARS=120,000 with an over-limit validation message; supported MIME list PROVIDER_SEND_TURN_SUPPORTED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES; expanded image dialog; drag-active overlay 'Drop files to attach'; attachment capability gated by supportsAttachmentUploads.
verevonRelevance: Client-side normalisation (HEIC, downscale to wire cap) before upload is cheap and avoids provider errors; Verevon should also extend beyond images to PDFs and audio, which T3 does not handle.
notes: Only images; no PDF/doc/audio/video upload or generation in this build. Quality 4: Robust client-side handling; images only, no other modalities.

name: Durable drafts and a cross-provider prompt stash
what: Unsent prompts, attachments and context chips persist per thread across reloads; Cmd/Ctrl+S stashes the current prompt (up to 20) so it can be moved to another thread or provider later.
how: composerDraftStore (zustand persist, key t3code:composer-drafts:v1, STORAGE_VERSION 8, 300 ms debounced localStorage with flush on beforeunload) keeps prompt, image attachments as data URLs, terminal contexts, element contexts, preview annotations, review comments and per-instance model selections; draft threads live client-side until the first send (routes _chat.draft.$draftId; finalizePromotedDraftThreadByRef); promptStashStore (key t3code:prompt-stash:v2, MAX_STASH_ENTRIES 20, attachment budget 2.7M chars, droppedImageNames/unreadableImageNames) is provider-agnostic by design and purges the v1 payload to protect the ~5 MB localStorage quota; keybinding composer.stash.
verevonRelevance: Draft durability with versioned migrations is table stakes; the stash (park a prompt, reuse elsewhere) is a nice-to-have that fits multi-agent workflows.
notes: Storage is localStorage-only; large images are dropped to stay under quota. Quality 4: Careful quota management and migrations; limited to localStorage.

name: Atomic thread bootstrap: create thread, prepare worktree, run setup script, start turn
what: Sending the first message from a draft creates the thread, optionally creates an isolated git worktree on a temporary branch, runs the project's setup script, then starts the turn as one operation; the title seeds from the first message and is later regenerated.
how: ChatView.onSend builds bootstrap {createThread{projectId,title,modelSelection,runtimeMode,interactionMode,branch,worktreePath,createdAt}, prepareWorktree{projectCwd, baseBranch, branch: buildTemporaryWorktreeBranchName(randomHex), startFromOrigin}, runSetupScript:true} and calls startThreadTurn with messageId, attachments, modelSelection, titleSeed, runtimeMode, interactionMode; titleSeed falls back to 'Image: name', terminal or element context labels, then 'New thread'; failures roll back the background-submission flag; persistThreadSettingsForNextTurn writes model/branch/mode first.
verevonRelevance: A single idempotent 'start run' command that provisions the sandbox/workspace and starts the turn simplifies Verevon's Model Plane run creation and avoids half-created sessions.
notes: Quality 4: Clean single command; depends on git worktrees.

name: Thread-scoped tabbed right panel (browser, terminal, diff, files, file, PR, agents)
what: Each thread has its own right-hand workspace with tabs: several browser tabs, terminals (with horizontal/vertical splits), a diff review, a file browser, individual file viewers, pull-request tabs and an agents roster; panel state is remembered per thread, can be maximized, and becomes a slide-over sheet on narrow windows.
how: rightPanelStore (zustand persist, key t3code:right-panel-state:v2, STORAGE_VERSION 11 with documented migrations) keeps byThreadKey {isOpen, activeSurfaceId, surfaces[]}; RightPanelSurface union ids browser:<tab>, terminal:<id> (terminalIds, activeTerminalId, splitDirection), diff, files, file:<path> (revealLine, revealRequestId), pull-request:<ref>, agents; actions open/openBrowser/openFile/openPullRequest/openTerminal/splitTerminal/closeOthers/closeToRight/closeAll/reconcileBrowserSurfaces/reconcileFileSurfaces; each feature owns its durable resource (preview tab ids, terminal session ids, workspace paths) - the store is intentionally a shallow descriptor list; RightPanelTabs adds a tab context menu (copy path, mute, close, close others, close to right, close all); RIGHT_PANEL_INLINE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY (max-width 980px) switches to RightPanelSheet (w-[min(42vw,28rem)]); keybindings rightPanel.toggle (mod+alt+b) and rightPanel.toggleMaximized; PanelLayoutControls badge shows live subagent count.
verevonRelevance: A per-thread 'workspace' of heterogeneous surfaces (document viewer, browser session, sandbox terminal, run trace) is exactly what Verevon agent pages need; keeping the store as descriptors that point at durable resources is a clean separation.
notes: The v9 note shows the 'plan' surface was removed because plans render inline in the transcript. Quality 4: Strong descriptor-based design with documented migrations; desktop-centric features inside.

name: Keyboard-first panel launcher with single-letter surface shortcuts
what: An empty right panel shows cards (Browser, Terminal, Files, Diff, Pull request, Agents); pressing B, T, F, D, P or A opens the surface from anywhere outside a typing context, arrows+Enter also work, and unavailable cards stay visible with a one-line reason.
how: RightPanelEmptyState with action list {shortcut: B|T|F|D|P|A, available}; surfaceShortcutActionForKey ignores events with meta/ctrl/alt, composing IME or defaultPrevented; surfaceShortcutTargetsTypingContext treats any focused editable (even empty composer) as typing; LAUNCHER_SHORTCUT_BLOCKING_LAYERS lists dialog/menu/select/popover/combobox/autocomplete slots that win over letters; SURFACE_UNAVAILABLE_HINTS give reasons ('Only available in the desktop app.', 'Available for Git repositories.').
verevonRelevance: Small delight: discoverable-but-fast surface opening without a palette; the typing-context guard is the key detail to copy.
notes: Quality 4: Small but carefully guarded against typing contexts.

name: Diff review panel with turn, branch and working-tree scopes
what: A diff panel lets the user review what the agent changed per turn, versus a base branch (automatic or chosen), or as uncommitted working-tree changes, in stacked or split view with word wrap, whitespace-ignore, collapse-all and per-file collapse remembered per scope.
how: DiffPanel (lazy chunk) with diffPanelStore selections {kind: branch{baseRef}|unstaged|turn{turnId,filePath,revealRequestId}} persisted per thread, DiffRenderMode stacked|split, base-ref combobox (buildBaseRefChoices/filterBaseRefChoices, AUTOMATIC_BASE_REF), collapse state keyed by scope (collapseScopeKey), refresh when a turn completes, review.getDiffPreview / review.getDiffFileContents RPCs, useCheckpointDiff for turn diffs (checkpoint refs), createGitDiffFileContentsLoader for lazy file bodies; rendering with @pierre/diffs CodeView in a worker pool (DiffWorkerPoolProvider) and theme names from resolveDiffThemeName; open-in-editor primary action per file (openDiffFilePrimaryAction).
verevonRelevance: Verevon is not an IDE, but any agent that edits documents, spreadsheets or records needs a per-run 'what changed' reviewer with scope switching; the turn-scope + base-scope model transfers.
notes: Heavy diff rendering is outsourced to @pierre/diffs (beta) with a worker pool. Quality 4: Comprehensive scopes and persistence; rendering depends on a beta third-party library.

name: Inline line comments on diffs and files that travel into the next prompt
what: Select lines in a diff or file, type a comment, and it is attached to the composer as a structured review comment that the agent receives with the next message; the same inline comment UI is reused for file previews, thread diffs and pull-request reviews.
how: AnnotatableCodeView wraps StyledDiffCodeView with DiffLineAnnotation groups per side/line; DiffCommentAnnotation (kinds draft|comment, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter submit via isCommentSubmitShortcut, Escape cancel, optional secondaryAction button); reviewCommentContext.ts serializes ReviewCommentContext {filePath, sectionId, range, text, diff, fenceLanguage, selection} to a <review_comment ...> XML-ish block with a fenced diff, and parses it back (REVIEW_COMMENT_BLOCK_PATTERN) so the user bubble re-renders as a comment card (UserMessageReviewCommentCard); stored in composerDraftStore.reviewComments and ComposerPendingReviewComments chips.
verevonRelevance: Anchored feedback on an artifact (a line, a cell, a paragraph) that becomes structured agent context is a strong pattern for Verevon document and report review.
notes: Quality 4: Unusual and well integrated into the prompt pipeline.

name: Provider-neutral tagged context blocks (terminal, element, annotation, review comment)
what: Things the user attaches beyond text - a terminal selection, a page element picked in the preview (with React component and source file), a screenshot annotation, a diff comment - show as chips in the composer and as cards in the sent message, but travel to any provider as plain tagged text.
how: lib/terminalContext.ts emits <terminal_context> blocks; lib/elementContext.ts emits <element_context> (pageUrl, tagName, selector, htmlPreview <=4000 chars, componentName, source frame, author styles <=4000 chars) and parses a trailing block back; lib/previewAnnotation.ts <preview_annotation>; reviewCommentContext.ts <review_comment>; extract functions strip blocks from message text for display and count them; drafts persist these in localStorage with strict clamping so a 5 MB outerHTML cannot break quota (normalizeElementContextSelection).
verevonRelevance: Encoding rich UI context as tagged text keeps Model Plane provider-agnostic and replayable; Verevon should define a small closed set of context tags with round-trip parsers.
notes: Parsing prose-embedded tags is fragile if a user types the same tags; the code anchors on trailing blocks and escapes attributes. Quality 4: Pragmatic and portable; relies on prose-embedded tags that could be spoofed.

name: 'Changed files' card under every assistant answer with smart auto-expand
what: Each answer that modified files ends with a compact card listing changed files with +/- counts, grouped into a directory tree; it opens automatically only when the latest turn touched five or fewer files and 200 or fewer changed lines, and clicking a file opens that turn's diff at that file.
how: AssistantChangedFilesSection reads TurnDiffSummary from useTurnDiffSummaries (event thread.turn.diff.complete / RPC orchestration.getTurnDiff); shouldAutoExpandChangedFiles with CHANGED_FILES_AUTO_EXPAND_FILE_LIMIT=5 and LINE_LIMIT=200; compact preview shows up to 3 files and 4 top-level scopes; ChangedFilesTree builds nested nodes with compactDirectoryNode (single-child chain collapse) and aggregated stats (turnDiffTree.ts); expansion persisted per thread+turn in uiStateStore.threadChangedFilesExpandedById; PierreEntryIcon file-type icons.
verevonRelevance: A standard 'what this run changed' footer with size-aware auto-expansion is a good default for any Verevon agent that mutates records or files.
notes: Quality 4: Smart size-aware defaults; coding-specific.

name: Subagent fleet view in the Agents panel
what: When the agent spawns subagents or workflows, the chat shows one 'Kicked off N subagents' call-to-action row per batch and the right-panel Agents tab shows the roster with fixed-height rows (identity, activity, metrics), per-agent model, tokens and elapsed time, with Working/Idle-resumable/Completed/Failed/Stopped states.
how: packages/client-runtime/state/subagentRuntime.ts folds persisted task.* and tool.* thread activities into RuntimeSubagent state (statuses pending, running, waiting, idle, completed, failed, cancelled, interrupted; SubagentUsage with max-merge for cumulative frames; activity ring buffer with consecutive-duplicate dedupe; first-write terminal timestamps; order-robust folding; sessionLive=false derives interruption) and deriveAgentPanelModel prefers an orchestration-v2 projection when available; AgentsPanel renders STATUS_VISUALS (all in-flight states show as one 'Working' state), workflow groups, DOM-write elapsed timers; WorkLogEntry.agentSpawn drives the CTA row (AgentSpawnCtaRow) and the toolbar badge via liveAgentCount.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a tested set of rules for presenting parallel agent runs (stable order, fixed row height, single 'working' state, resumable idle) distilled from live-test feedback. Baseline check: Verevon's Fleet run console cannot load data (no gateway route) and subagent lineage is only partially shown; T3's fixed-row, single-'Working'-state rules are directly reusable.
notes: File header says it is legacy-bridge code until orchestration-v2 replaces the fold. Quality 4: Rules distilled from live testing; implemented as a legacy fold awaiting orchestration v2.

name: Agent-visible in-app browser with controller indicator, cursor and PiP mini player
what: When the agent drives the built-in browser, the preview shows an 'Agent controlling browser' badge, a synthetic cursor that follows the agent's pointer events (dimmer when a human has control), and a draggable, resizable picture-in-picture mini player can pop up automatically so the user can watch from any panel.
how: PreviewView reads desktopOverlay.controller (human|agent|none) and renders AgentBrowserCursor (CURSOR_ACTIVE_MS=700, opacity 1 when active else 0.18 human / 0.35 otherwise) from browserPointerStore events (desktop:preview-pointer-event); ThreadPreviewMiniPlayer with pointer-drag/resize state and clamp helpers (previewMiniPlayerLayout); setting browserAutoShowFloatingPreview (default true; an explicit open/show on preview_open still wins); BrowserSurfaceSlot keeps a Chromium <webview> mounted across panel changes; viewport presets (iPhone SE ... Galaxy Z Fold 5, Nest Hub) and PREVIEW_VIEWPORT 240..3840 px; screen recording via MediaRecorder; webviewCrashRecovery.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon computer-use the human/agent control indicator, visible cursor and a follow-along mini player are the trust-building UI basics; Quarry's browser runs remotely, so the stream would be a screencast rather than a local webview. Baseline check: a Verevon chat turn cannot drive a browser today (baseline known gap 8) and Quarry executes remotely; a controller badge, visible cursor and screencast PiP would fit that remote model.
notes: Desktop-only (Electron webview); the web build shows 'Preview is desktop-only'. Quality 4: Strong trust cues (controller badge, cursor, PiP); desktop-only webview.

name: Pull-request workspace: list, detail tabs and batched review with verdict
what: A Pull requests page lists changes across projects with filters, opens each in a right-panel tab (summary, timeline, checks, code), and lets the user write line comments plus a summary and send them in one review as Comment, Approve or Request changes; a thread can be created from a PR.
how: routes/_chat.pull-requests.tsx (88KB) paginates per-environment with continuation cursors; components/pullRequest/* (23 files) include PullRequestDetailPanel, SummaryTab, TimelineTab, ChecksPopover, ReviewerPicker, Reactions, MarkdownEditor; PullRequestCodeTab (lazy) reuses AnnotatableCodeView; pullRequestReviewStore holds in-memory draft comments and summary per project/repository#number (deliberately not persisted because a review is one request carrying all comments and the verdict); PullRequestReviewBar VERDICTS comment|approve|request-changes; git.resolvePullRequest and git.preparePullRequestThread create a thread bound to the PR branch/worktree; providers GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket.
verevonRelevance: Mostly coding-specific; the transferable part is the batched-review store (comments held until one submit with a verdict) for approval workflows over agent output.
notes: Out of scope for a non-IDE product, but shows how far T3 goes beyond chat. Quality 4: Extensive for a chat app; coding-specific and outside Verevon's scope.

name: Context-aware, user-editable keybinding system (when-clauses, conflicts, per-project scripts)
what: Every action has a default shortcut, can be rebound in a Keybindings page (record a key press, edit a 'when' condition), conflicts are flagged, and project scripts can get their own shortcuts; shortcut hints appear in tooltips and as hold-to-reveal badges for thread and model jumps.
how: contracts/keybindings.ts defines KeybindingCommand (static ids such as sidebar.toggle, terminal.*, rightPanel.*, diff.toggle, preview.*, commandPalette.toggle, filePicker.toggle, projectSearch.toggle, themeEditor.toggle, composer.stash, chat.new/newLocal, editor.openFavorite, modelPicker.*, thread.* plus pattern script.<id>.run), KeybindingRule {key, command, when} with a when-expression AST (identifier/not/and/or, depth cap 64) and a 256-rule cap; shared/keybindings.ts holds DEFAULT_KEYBINDINGS (mod+b sidebar, mod+j terminal, mod+k palette, mod+p file picker, mod+shift+f content search, mod+d diff, mod+shift+j preview, mod+shift+m model picker, mod+n chat.new, mod+shift+[/] thread prev/next, mod+1..9 thread jump or model jump when modelPickerOpen); client keybindings.resolveShortcutCommand scans the list from the end so later (user) rules win, with a context {terminalFocus, terminalOpen, previewFocus, previewOpen, ...}; KeybindingsSettings.logic builds rows with source Default|Custom|Project, conflict labels via conflictsWithWhen, keybindingFromKeyboardEvent for capture, when-variable autocomplete; server persists keybindings.json and exposes RPC server.upsertKeybinding/removeKeybinding; decode is forward-compatible (unknown commands are dropped, not fatal).
verevonRelevance: VS Code-style context keys with last-rule-wins and a conflict-aware editor give power users parity with desktop AI tools; portable to Solid because the engine is pure functions over a rule list. Baseline check: Verevon has a small fixed shortcut set (use-chat-shortcuts.ts: new chat, focus composer, thread switch) with no customization or conflict handling.
notes: Hold-to-show jump hints use a 200 ms delay (THREAD_JUMP_HINT_SHOW_DELAY_MS). Quality 5: Best-in-class for a web chat app: when-clauses, last-rule-wins, conflict detection and forward-compatible decoding.

name: Searchable settings with anchored scroll, pulse highlight and per-setting reset
what: Settings has eight sections (General, Appearance, Keybindings, Providers, Integrations, Source Control, Connections, Archive) and a global settings search that jumps to the exact row, scrolls it into view, focuses it and pulses it; each changed setting shows an undo-to-default button.
how: settingsSearch.ts SETTINGS_SEARCH_ITEMS (about 40 entries: Color scheme, Themes, Contrast, Glass opacity, Environment identification, four font settings, Font smoothing, Word wrap, Project grouping, Auto-settle, Time format, Hide whitespace changes, Skills in slash menu, Provider update checks, New threads, Start from origin, Archive/Delete confirmation, Hold to quit, Text generation model, Diagnostics, Plan mode (legacy), Stream token by token (legacy), Sidebar (legacy), Agent browser access, Default browser viewport/zoom/appearance, Auto-show floating preview, Remote environments, Archived threads) is the single source for anchor ids and titles ('so a retitle or translation pass happens once'); desktopOnly flag hides results that have no anchor on web; SettingsSearchTargetProvider scrolls with smooth behaviour unless prefers-reduced-motion and adds a settings-search-target-pulse class; SettingResetButton (Undo2Icon) and PolicyTooltip in settingsLayout.tsx; settings nav renders from SETTINGS_SECTION_LABELS; SettingsSidebarNav swaps in for the thread sidebar on /settings.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's many admin and personal settings need the same searchable catalog with deep-link anchors; defining titles once also prepares i18n (T3 has no i18n yet).
notes: Legacy toggles (plan mode, token-by-token streaming, legacy sidebar) are labelled in the UI as legacy, a transparent way to retire behaviour. Quality 4: Single-source catalog with anchored pulse highlight is polished; legacy toggles linger.

name: Snapshot-then-resume sync with sequence dedupe and windowed history
what: The client renders instantly from a cached snapshot, loads the fresh snapshot over compressible HTTP, then opens a WebSocket stream that resumes exactly after the snapshot's sequence; very long threads load only the last N user turns and fetch older pages on demand without duplicating streaming text.
how: OrchestrationSubscribeShellInput/ThreadInput accept afterSequence (server replays events after it, or sends a fallback snapshot if the gap is too large), requestCompletionMarker (explicit end-of-catch-up marker) and turnLimit; shellSnapshotHttp and threadSnapshotHttp fetch snapshots over HTTP with bounded timeouts (cached state renders while waiting) and only send windows to servers that advertise threadSnapshotPagination; OrchestrationThreadDetailWindow {turnLimit, beforeCursor opaque exclusive}; page {beforeCursor, hasMore, snapshotSequence, threadSequence} where threadSequence is a per-thread watermark that must be applied before merging an older page so a streaming turn outside the window is not double-applied; pure reducers shellReducer/threadReducer shared by web and mobile; unknown events leave the snapshot reference unchanged.
verevonRelevance: This is a model protocol for Verevon's realtime chat/agent streams (Application Plane projections): snapshot over HTTP, resume by sequence, per-aggregate watermark and capability-gated pagination. Baseline check: Verevon resumes SSE with Last-Event-ID from a 10-minute in-memory buffer that is lost on gateway restart; a durable per-aggregate sequence (T3) removes that weakness.
notes: Capability advertisement (threadSnapshotPagination) is how old servers and new clients coexist. Quality 5: Best-in-class protocol detail: per-thread watermark, capability-gated windows and gap fallback.

name: Shell vs detail projections keep the sidebar cheap
what: The sidebar never loads full threads: it subscribes to a lightweight 'shell' of projects and thread summaries (status flags, latest turn, pin/snooze/settle fields, plan step progress), while opening a thread subscribes to its detail.
how: OrchestrationThreadShell carries id, projectId, title, modelSelection, runtimeMode, interactionMode, branch, worktreePath, linkedPullRequest, latestTurn, archivedAt, settledOverride/settledAt, snoozedUntil, pinnedAt/pinOrderKey, session, latestUserMessageAt, hasPendingApprovals, hasPendingUserInput, hasActionableProposedPlan, backgroundLiveness, planProgress{step,completedSteps,totalSteps}; OrchestrationThread is the detail with messages, activities, proposed plans and checkpoints; threadDetail.ts merges them noting that shell wins for branch/worktree/project to avoid targeting a stale checkout after reconnect; SIDEBAR_THREAD_PREWARM_LIMIT=3 prewarms the first visible thread details.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's agent list should be driven by a precomputed summary projection (attention flags, progress step) separate from full run transcripts, so lists scale to thousands of runs.
notes: Quality 4: Clean separation that keeps lists cheap; standard in principle.

name: One UI, many environments: primary, paired bearer, managed relay and SSH targets
what: A single window can show projects and threads from the local machine, other paired computers, a cloud relay, SSH hosts and WSL distributions; every thread URL carries an environment id and the connection supervisor retries with typed transient/blocked reasons and wakes on app activation.
how: client-runtime/connection/model.ts tagged classes PrimaryConnectionTarget, BearerConnectionTarget, RelayConnectionTarget, SshConnectionTarget (Persisted* excludes Primary) and ConnectionTransientReason network|timeout|transport|endpoint-unavailable|relay-unavailable|remote-unavailable with a Blocked reason set; supervisor.ts (819 lines) manages connections; ConnectionWakeups application-active|application-active-probe|application-active-reconnect|credentials-changed trigger resubscribe; capabilities services (CloudSession, RelayDeviceIdentity, SshEnvironmentGateway) are Effect Context services injected per platform; ScopedThreadRef/ScopedProjectRef pair environmentId with ids because ids are only unique per environment; connections settings page and CloudEnvironmentConnectList; remote access via pairing links (token in URL fragment) and Tailscale.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is multi-tenant/multi-region; scoping every ref by environment and modelling connection health as typed states is directly useful, and a relay-style target maps to Verevon's gateway.
notes: Platform services are injected (Effect Context), which makes the same runtime run on web, Electron and mobile. Quality 4: Rare and thorough; Effect-based runtime adds complexity.

name: State management: Effect atoms for server state, versioned zustand stores for UI state
what: Server-derived state (threads, projects, settings, provider snapshots, PRs) lives in Effect atoms with an atom registry; UI-only state (right panel surfaces, diff selection, composer drafts, prompt stash, UI expansion, terminal UI, preview mini player) lives in small zustand stores whose persisted shapes carry explicit versions and migrations.
how: @effect/atom-react (useAtomValue, useAtomCommand, AtomCommandResult, appAtomRegistry); keys and versions: t3code:right-panel-state:v2 (storage version 11), t3code:composer-drafts:v1 (version 8), t3code:prompt-stash:v2, t3code:ui-state:v1 (legacy keys renderer-state v3..v8 and codething:renderer-state v1..v4 purged), diffPanelStore persist, terminalUiStateStore, previewStateStore, previewMiniPlayerStore; a TanStack Pacer Debouncer batches UI-state writes; useLocalStorage wraps Schema-validated keys; TanStack Router file-based routes with beforeLoad auth gate redirecting to /pair; useSyncExternalStore for viewport width.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Solid signals/stores: keep server state in a query layer keyed by aggregate and UI state in small persisted stores with schema versions, and delete legacy keys on boot to protect the 5 MB quota.
notes: Heavy reliance on Effect (4.0 beta) makes the code idiomatic only inside that ecosystem; for Verevon the transferable part is the layering, not the library. Quality 4: Sound layering with versioned persisted stores; heavy Effect dependency.

name: Performance toolkit: virtualization, lazy surfaces, mount caps and structural sharing
what: The UI stays fast with huge threads and many open surfaces: virtualized message list, lazily loaded Diff/Preview/File panels and syntax-highlighter languages, capped hidden terminals and previews, worker-based diff rendering, LRU caches and per-row memoization.
how: LegendList virtualization (patched @legendapp/list 3.3.5) in MessagesTimeline and the model picker; React.lazy for PreviewPanel, DiffPanel, FilePreviewPanel, PullRequestCodeTab; separate chunks for 100+ Shiki languages and themes; MAX_HIDDEN_MOUNTED_TERMINAL_THREADS=10 and MAX_HIDDEN_MOUNTED_PREVIEW_THREADS=3 keep recent threads' terminals/previews mounted but bound the rest; DiffWorkerPoolProvider and worker chunk (worker-CIcqvLjo.js); LRUCache for highlighted HTML with estimated byte size; useStableRows/computeStableMessagesTimelineRows reuse unchanged row references; self-ticking WorkingTimer and LiveElapsed write DOM text directly so streaming does not commit React every second; Ghostty VT WASM terminal renderer; SIDEBAR_THREAD_PREWARM_LIMIT=3.
evidence: ev_c4296b0b3e57b255897c980d2722151300d0cacf0f9ff08751a9887f8e23af99 (REA analyze_javascript_application over the shipped SPA chunks index, textarea, FilePreviewPanel and worker: 4 files parsed, 8.0 MB text, 1,320 module nodes recovered from bundler factories, partial semantic coverage; confirms the code-split chunk layout)
verevonRelevance: A checklist for Verevon's Solid UI: virtualize timelines, lazy-load heavy surfaces, bound hidden mounts, and avoid per-second re-renders for timers.
notes: Quality 4: Comprehensive and pragmatic; typical of a mature React app.

name: Accessibility and input-modality handling
what: The UI honours reduced motion in several animations, forced-colors mode, coarse-pointer font sizing (prevents iOS zoom), keyboard reachability of hover-only actions, tooltips that include shortcut labels, aria-labels on icon buttons and roles on custom widgets.
how: prefers-reduced-motion checks in draftHeroTransition, ChatView, BranchToolbar, settingsLayout, SidebarUpdatePill and the Ghostty terminal surface (steady cursor), plus 4 reduced-motion and 4 forced-colors blocks in the built CSS; one rule forces font-size max(prompt size,16px) on coarse pointers under 40rem; hover-revealed controls also use focus-within; Tooltip popups append shortcutLabelForCommand; aria-pressed/aria-expanded on toggles; progressbar role on the context meter; sr-only labels on compact buttons; about 149 SPA files use aria-* (scout); Base UI primitives supply focus management.
verevonRelevance: Sets a practical accessibility baseline (motion, contrast, pointer, keyboard) that Verevon should meet or exceed; no screen-reader or i18n work was found, so there is room to lead. Baseline check: Verevon already ships no/en i18n and screen-reader live-region narration that T3 lacks; keep those while adopting T3's pointer, motion and forced-colors rules.
notes: No automated accessibility tests were observed; no i18n framework (strings are inline English). Quality 4: Good baseline but partial reduced-motion coverage and no tests or i18n observed.

name: Slow-request toast with expandable request list
what: If a backend request is still unacknowledged after 15 seconds (2 minutes for install-style calls), a persistent toast appears listing which requests are waiting and since when, and disappears when they finish.
how: rpc/requestLatencyState tracks pending requests in an atom (SLOW_RPC_ACK_THRESHOLD_MS=15000, LONG_RUNNING_RPC_ACK_THRESHOLD_MS=120000, MAX_TRACKED_RPC_ACK_REQUESTS=256) with per-method exemptions (previewAutomationConnect) and long-running methods (server.updateProvider/refreshProviders/updateServer); SlowRpcRequestToastCoordinator renders a toast with expandableContent describing each request tag and start time.
verevonRelevance: A cheap, honest way to surface backend stalls instead of spinners; Verevon could show planes and methods involved.
notes: Quality 4: Simple and honest; unique small feature.

name: Usage and cost page across providers, built from local transcripts
what: A Usage page charts token and cost usage per provider over time, including turns that ran outside the app, with provider plan detection.
how: routes/usage.tsx and components/usage/UsagePage.tsx (27KB) + UsageProviderChart; shared usageFormat/usageMerge; server UsageService reads provider transcript files (Claude project transcripts, Codex sessions) with usagePricing tables and caching (approach credited to ccusage in a module comment); RPC server.getUsageSummary; contracts/usage.ts.
verevonRelevance: Per-user, per-model cost transparency is a headline Verevon feature; T3 derives it after the fact from transcripts, Verevon can meter at the Model Plane instead. Baseline check: Verevon already has per-answer cost badges and a cost-core dashboard; the missing piece is a live spend meter, which T3 does not have either.
notes: Server file cited from scout inventory; SPA and shared files verified. Quality 4: Useful but derived after the fact from transcripts rather than metered live.

name: Driver SPI: provider instances as plain-value closures (snapshot, adapter, text generation)
what: Each backend (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode) is a driver that, per configured instance, yields three isolated capabilities: a health/model snapshot probe, a session/turn adapter, and a text-generation service; instances of the same driver share no mutable state and can be reloaded independently.
how: ProviderDriver<Config,R> record {driverKind, metadata{displayName, supportsMultipleInstances}, configSchema: Schema.Codec decoded once by the registry, create(input)} returns ProviderInstance {instanceId, driverKind, continuationIdentity{driverKind, continuationKey default '<kind>:instance:<id>'}, displayName, accentColor, enabled, snapshot, adapter, textGeneration}; builtInDrivers.BUILT_IN_DRIVERS = [Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode]; unknown or failed-decode drivers become unavailable shadow snapshots (buildUnavailableProviderSnapshot); ProviderInstanceRegistry owns the live Map<InstanceId, ProviderInstance>, hydrated from ServerSettings.providerInstances with mutator for live edits; adding a driver = new Drivers/<Name>Driver.ts + one array entry.
verevonRelevance: A clean seam for Model Plane in Rust: a driver trait producing per-instance (probe, session adapter, utility-model client) objects with typed config decoded once; unavailable shadow instances keep data round-trippable.
notes: ContinuationIdentity is what the UI exposes as continuation.groupKey; instances sharing a key can swap mid-thread. Quality 5: Best-in-class seam: plain-value closures, per-instance isolation and typed config decode.

name: Canonical provider runtime event stream normalising five agent protocols
what: Whatever the backend (Codex app-server JSON-RPC, Claude Agent SDK, OpenCode SDK, Cursor/Grok over ACP), the app sees one vocabulary of events (session, thread, turn, item, content delta, request/approval, user-input, task, hook, tool progress, token usage, rate limits, MCP status, model rerouted, deprecation notice, runtime error) with the raw provider payload retained for debugging.
how: contracts/providerRuntime.ts: ProviderRuntimeEventType (48 literals, e.g. session.started, thread.token-usage.updated, turn.plan.updated, turn.proposed.delta, turn.diff.updated, item.started/updated/completed, content.delta with RuntimeContentStreamKind assistant_text|reasoning_text|reasoning_summary_text|plan_text|command_output|file_change_output, request.opened/resolved, user-input.requested/resolved, task.*, hook.*, tool.progress, tool.summary, account.rate-limits.updated, mcp.status.updated, model.rerouted, config.warning, deprecation.notice, runtime.warning/error); CanonicalItemType (user_message, assistant_message, reasoning, plan, command_execution, file_change, mcp_tool_call, dynamic_tool_call, collab_agent_tool_call, web_search, image_view, review_entered/exited, context_compaction, error); CanonicalRequestType (command_execution_approval, file_read_approval, file_change_approval, apply_patch_approval, exec_command_approval, mcp_elicitation_approval, tool_user_input, dynamic_tool_call, auth_tokens_refresh); RuntimeEventRaw.source union (codex.app-server.notification|request, codex.eventmsg, claude.sdk.message|permission, codex.sdk.thread-event, opencode.sdk.event, acp.jsonrpc, acp.<vendor>.extension); ProviderService.streamEvents fans out one Stream<ProviderRuntimeEvent>.
