verevonRelevance: The most reusable artifact for Model Plane: a provider-neutral run-event taxonomy (with reasoning stream kinds, approvals, task/hook events and a raw-payload escape hatch) that the Verevon chat and agent pages can both render. Baseline check: Verevon's model-gateway ChatEvent enum already covers chunk, reasoning_delta, tool_call, awaiting_approval, citation, plan_proposed and usage; compare against T3's item/task/hook/request taxonomy and fill granularity gaps.
notes: Raw payload is kept per event, supporting deep debugging and replay (EventNdjsonLogger per provider session). Quality 5: Best-in-class: one taxonomy over five protocols with raw payload retained.

name: Mid-thread model switching via capability flags and session restart with resume cursor
what: Changing the model during a conversation just works for providers that support in-session switching; for others the server transparently restarts the provider session (resuming where possible), and some providers explicitly require a new thread.
how: ProviderAdapterCapabilities.sessionModelSwitch is 'in-session' (Claude and Codex adapters) or 'unsupported'; ProviderCommandReactor compares requested vs active session (runtimeMode, cwd, instance, model) and restarts the session when needed, passing resumeCursor only when the model did not change on an unsupported adapter; Claude also restarts on any model selection change; Grok sets requiresNewThreadForModelChange: true which the SPA turns into the 'Start a new chat to change models' toast; turn-level modelSelection overrides are normalised so unsupported adapters keep the active model unless an explicit selection arrives.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should model 'can this session hot-swap models?' as an explicit capability and own the restart/replay logic server-side rather than leaving it to the UI.
notes: Line numbers from recovered server tree; behaviour verified in source. Quality 4: Capability-flag design is sound; behaviour differs per adapter and is documented only in code.

name: Remote-updatable model manifest to mark current vs legacy models
what: Which models appear as current versus under 'Legacy models' is controlled by a small manifest that refreshes from the project's main branch once an hour, so a new model can be promoted without shipping a release; a failed fetch never breaks provider checks.
how: ModelManifest.ts: MODEL_MANIFEST_URL (raw.githubusercontent.com .../apps/server/src/provider/model-manifest.json), MANIFEST_TTL_MS 1h, MANIFEST_RETRY_MS 5 min, FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 10s, schema {version:1, currentModels: Record<driverKind,string[]>} (builds only accept versions they understand); preference remote, then last successful on-disk copy, then the bundled JSON; drivers call applyModelManifest on every snapshot draft path (pending, probe, error fallbacks) so classification is uniform.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's model catalog should be data-driven and hot-updatable (with signed, versioned config) so deprecations and launches do not need frontend or Model Plane releases.
notes: Trust boundary: remote config from a public branch steers UI classification only, but the same pattern for prompts or tools would be risky. Quality 4: Neat operationally; remote config from a public branch is a trust consideration.

name: Utility-model service for titles, commit messages and PR text
what: A cheaper 'utility' model (separately selectable per provider) names threads, writes commit messages, branch names and PR descriptions; title prompts aim at a name you will recognise weeks later, can be regenerated (individually or in bulk from the sidebar) and respect a configurable writing style.
how: TextGeneration service per provider instance (Claude/Codex/Cursor/Grok/OpenCode TextGeneration.ts); TextGenerationPrompts builds JSON-only prompts: buildCommitMessagePrompt, buildPrContentPrompt, buildBranchNamePrompt, buildThreadTitlePrompt with INITIAL and regenerate variants that pass the previous title and instruct to replace generic or artifact-based titles and to exclude models, tools and formats unless they are the topic; presets default|conventional_commits|repo_conventions|custom (TextGenerationPresets, SourceControlWritingStyleSettings with followChangeRequestTemplates); settings textGenerationModelSelection (default codex gpt-5.6-luna with reasoningEffort low) and sourceControlWriterModelSelection; thread.title.regeneration.complete event and a bulk 'regenerate titles' sidebar context menu item.
verevonRelevance: Auto-titling that targets later recognisability, with regenerate-on-demand and a distinct cheap model, is a quality-of-life feature Verevon should copy for chat and agent run lists.
notes: Quality 4: Good prompt design and policy presets.

name: Split client-local vs server-authoritative settings with defaults-by-decoding
what: Appearance and sidebar preferences stay per client, while anything that changes server behaviour (provider instances, agent browser access, text-generation models, background activity, git defaults) is server-authoritative so desktop and phone attached to one server never disagree.
how: contracts/settings.ts ClientSettingsSchema (appearance, sidebar, confirmations, favorites, providerModelPreferences, browser defaults) versus ServerSettings (enableLegacyTokenStreaming, enableProviderUpdateChecks, enableAgentBrowserAccess, backgroundActivity profile balanced|performance|battery-saver|custom with overrides, defaultThreadEnvMode, newWorktreesStartFromOrigin, addProjectBaseDirectory, textGenerationModelSelection, sourceControlWritingStyle, providers (legacy), providerInstances, observability); every field uses Schema.withDecodingDefault so decoding {} yields DEFAULT_*_SETTINGS; renamed keys are deliberately 'fresh' so decoding drops the old key and resets to the new default; ServerSettingsPatch / ClientSettingsPatch deep-partial types; ServerSettingsOperation enum; server.getSettings/updateSettings RPC and settings.json under the state dir.
verevonRelevance: Same split fits Verevon (user preference vs org/space policy); defaults-by-decode is a neat way to guarantee forward-compatible settings in Rust with serde defaults.
notes: Quality 4: Disciplined and forward-compatible.

name: Server-authoritative agent-capability gate that removes both the tool and its prompt text
what: Turning off agent browser access withholds the tool credential and also drops the prompt text that describes those tools, so the model never learns the capability exists; the user's own browser panel is unaffected.
how: ServerSettings.enableAgentBrowserAccess (default true): when false the MCP credential is not attached, the 't3-code' MCP server and every preview_* tool are never exposed to the provider session, and the prompt text describing them is omitted; documented as server-authoritative because tool injection and prompt construction happen on the server and must not differ between clients; related client setting browserAutoShowFloatingPreview.
verevonRelevance: Capability gating must remove tools and the prompt mentions together; Verevon's per-space tool policy should be enforced at prompt/tool assembly in Model Plane, never in the client.
notes: Default is enabled (opt-out), which is permissive for a browser-control capability. Quality 4: Correct removal of tool and prompt text; default is opt-out.

name: Default runtime mode is Full access
what: New threads default to the most permissive runtime mode (commands and edits without prompts) unless the user picks Supervised, Auto-accept edits or Auto in the composer footer.
how: DEFAULT_RUNTIME_MODE = 'full-access' in contracts/orchestration.ts; RuntimeMode literals approval-required, auto-accept-edits, auto, full-access; applied on thread creation and every turn; server maps modes to provider-native permission modes.
verevonRelevance: A cautionary data point: Verevon's defaults for agent autonomy should be policy-driven and conservative for enterprise tenants rather than permissive by default.
notes: Quality 2 reflects the default choice, not the implementation of the modes. Quality 2: Mode implementation is fine but the permissive default is a governance weakness.

name: Design-system stack: Base UI primitives, CVA variants, Tailwind v4 tokens, glass surfaces
what: All controls come from one in-repo component kit (button, menu, popover, select, combobox, dialog, sheet, tooltip, toast, switch, toggle-group, scroll-area, kbd, empty state, sidebar) built on headless Base UI with class-variance-authority variants and Tailwind v4 semantic tokens; touch targets are taller below the sm breakpoint and shrink to dense desktop sizes above it.
how: components/ui (35 files) wrap @base-ui/react (useRender, mergeProps); button.tsx defines sizes compact, default (h-9 sm:h-8), icon, icon-lg, icon-micro, icon-sm, icon-xl, icon-xs, lg, micro, sm, xl, xs and variants default, destructive, destructive-outline, ghost, ghost-muted, glass (surface-glass), link, outline, secondary with inset highlight shadows and --control-radius; data-slot attributes ('button', 'popover-popup', 'menu-popup', 'select-popup', 'combobox-popup', 'dialog-popup') are used by global keyboard guards; lucide-react icons; Tailwind 4.3.0 build uses @layer theme/base/components/utilities and oklch custom properties with color-mix for alpha variants; glass tokens --glass-blur 12px, --glass-opacity 80%, --glass-saturation 1.14; --workspace-topbar-height 52px and titlebar control tokens.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Solid frontend can adopt the same recipe (headless primitives + variant recipes + semantic oklch tokens) using Kobalte/Ark equivalents; the data-slot convention is a cheap way to coordinate global keyboard handling across popups.
notes: Looks like a shadcn-derived kit adapted to Base UI (file names and structure match); upstream name not stated in the files. Quality 4: Mature and consistent kit; standard stack choices.

name: Thread-scoped stacked toasts with expandable detail and copy-for-errors
what: Toasts stack in a corner, collapse the older ones behind the front toast, can expand to show details (for example slow requests), carry a bottom action row, and thread-scoped toasts only appear while the user is looking at that thread.
how: ui/toast.tsx (Base UI toast manager, default position top-right) with ThreadToastData {threadRef, actionLayout 'stacked-end', actionVariant, expandableContent, expandableDescriptionTrigger}; shouldRenderThreadScopedToast(data, activeThreadRef) filters by the route's active thread (useActiveThreadRefFromRoute); toast.logic.ts buildVisibleToastLayout/shouldHideCollapsedToastContent compute stack offsets and keep the front-most readable; stackedThreadToast helper forces the stacked action layout; hiddenToastActionProps removes a CTA on update; types error|warning|success|info|loading with priority and timeout.
verevonRelevance: Per-run toasts that only show in the relevant run view avoid cross-talk when several agents run at once.
notes: Quality 4: Thoughtful scoping and layout.

name: Composer-attached banner stack and provider status banner
what: Warnings and notices (provider needs login, update available, reconnecting) dock above the composer as a stack with the front banner readable and the next one peeking behind it in its severity colour; provider problems also float over the timeline without moving content.
how: ComposerBannerStack animates dismissal (DISMISS_TRANSITION_MS 220, translate3d exit) and colours the stack cap by the first hidden banner's variant (default|error|info|success|warning); items carry id, variant, urgent, icon, title, description, actions, dismissLabel; ProviderStatusBanner is keyed by hash of (instanceId, status, auth status, message) so a dismissal only holds for that exact condition, shows 'is unauthenticated - Sign in via the CLI to authenticate again' for error+unauthenticated, rendered absolutely over the timeline (pointer-events-none wrapper) so layout is stable; ThreadErrorBanner dismissal is per session; ThreadSyncStatusPill shows sync phase.
verevonRelevance: Condition-keyed dismissal and non-shifting overlays are good patterns for connector auth failures and quota notices in Verevon.
notes: There is no in-app login for providers; the banner tells users to authenticate in the provider CLI. Quality 4: Condition-keyed dismissal and non-shifting overlays are well done.

name: Canvas terminal on Ghostty VT WASM with 'Add to chat' selections
what: Terminals per thread render on a canvas using Ghostty's VT parser compiled to WASM, with correct IME, link detection, Nerd Font glyph fallback and scrollback anchoring; selecting text offers 'Add to chat' (inserts a terminal-context chip) or Copy, and right-click offers Paste.
how: terminal/ghostty/{core.ts (WASM runtime wrapper), renderer.ts, surface.ts (72KB), runtime.ts, keyCodes.ts}; bundled SymbolsNerdFontMono woff2 fallback stack; CURSOR_BLINK_INTERVAL_MS 500 with steady hollow cursor when unfocused or reduced motion; grid anchors to the bottom once scrollback exists; hidden textarea bridges clipboard and IME; terminal-links.ts extracts wrapped links (openable in the preview via openTerminalLinkInPreview); ThreadTerminalDrawer selection popup items add-to-chat/copy and context menu paste; lib/terminalContext builds <terminal_context> blocks (expired contexts with no text are dropped); server terminal Manager uses node-pty (ConPTY on Windows) with thread-scoped sessions; RPC terminal.open/new/split/attach/write/resize/clear/restart/close; terminalCloseConfirm warns when a subprocess is running.
verevonRelevance: Verevon sandboxes need a terminal view; a WASM VT core (ghostty-vt) rendered on canvas works in the browser and in a Rust-native future, and 'Add to chat' is a nice selection-to-context affordance.
notes: Heavy custom code (renderer, selection, IME) is the cost of not using xterm.js. Quality 4: Impressive custom engine; high maintenance and desktop-heavy.

name: Hold-to-quit guard protecting running agents
what: Pressing the quit shortcut only shows a 'Hold to Quit' hint; quitting requires holding it (about 1.2 s) or double-tapping within 500 ms, so a stray Cmd/Ctrl+Q does not kill running agent sessions; menu Quit still quits immediately and the guard can be disabled.
how: desktop window/QuitHold.ts makeQuitHoldHandler on Electron before-input-event (runs before the native accelerator) with QUIT_HOLD_DURATION_MS 1200, QUIT_DOUBLE_TAP_MS 500, QUIT_HOLD_RELEASE_GRACE_MS 600; 'still held' is proven by auto-repeat keydowns because macOS suppresses the Q keyUp while Command is down; notify('down'|'up') drives the renderer's QuitHoldOverlay; setting confirmQuit (default true); IPC and overlay component QuitHoldOverlay.tsx.
verevonRelevance: Desktop-only, but the principle (guard destructive global shortcuts when long-running work is live) applies to Verevon's PWA close/refresh prompts for running agents.
notes: Quality 4: Careful key-event engineering; desktop-only.

name: Native-feeling desktop chrome and boot splash that matches the theme
what: The Electron shell uses an inset title bar on macOS (traffic lights placed at 16,18) and a window-controls overlay elsewhere, enforces a minimum window of 840x620, and paints a theme-coloured splash from an inline boot script before React mounts so there is no white flash.
how: DesktopWindow.getWindowTitleBarOptions (titleBarStyle hiddenInset + trafficLightPosition on darwin; hidden + titleBarOverlay updated by setTitleBarOverlay when theme changes elsewhere); CSS tokens --workspace-controls-left/right/top, --workspace-native-controls-inset and the 'wco:' Tailwind variant for env(titlebar-area-height); AppSidebarLayout reserves MACOS_TRAFFIC_LIGHTS_LEFT_INSET 90px unless fullscreen via desktop:get/onWindowFullscreenStateChange; index.html inline script reads t3code:themes:v1, theme-follow-system, theme-appearance-mode, theme-halves keys and sets SPLASH_COLORS and built-in palette values before mount; PWA manifest (display standalone, theme_color #161616) and viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content for phones.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's web/PWA should adopt the boot-time theme paint and viewport settings; native chrome details matter if a Tauri/Electron wrapper is planned.
notes: The same SPA is served to browsers and phones by the server, so web polish and desktop polish share code. Quality 4: Polished and standard.

name: Responsive behaviour: sheet panels, offcanvas sidebar and mobile composer rules
what: On narrow windows the right panel becomes a slide-over sheet and the sidebar becomes off-canvas; on phones Enter inserts a newline instead of sending, the composer can force-expand, inputs are at least 16 px, and a mobile View Transition animates the composer.
how: RIGHT_PANEL_INLINE_LAYOUT_MEDIA_QUERY '(max-width: 980px)' selects RightPanelSheet (w-[min(42vw,28rem)] / max-[760px] w-[min(88vw,24rem)]); Sidebar collapsible='offcanvas' with useSidebar().isMobile and setOpenMobile; composerSubmissionIntentForEnter returns null when isMobileViewport; forceExpandedMobileComposer prop; runMobileComposerTransition (View Transitions API, (max-width: 639px)); CSS rule font-size:max(var(--font-size-prompt),16px) for (width<=39.999rem) and (pointer:coarse); hover-only affordances are gated by @media (hover:hover); BranchToolbar collapses labels to icons with a measured hysteresis; useMediaQuery hook.
verevonRelevance: Mobile-web parity is a stated Verevon target; these specific rules (Enter semantics, 16px inputs, hover gating, sheet panels) are the practical checklist.
notes: A separate Expo/React Native app exists in the monorepo (not in this build) and shares client-runtime and theme roles. Quality 4: Practical rules applied consistently; some features remain desktop-only.

name: Context-aware git primary action with staged progress and worktree-per-thread
what: A single git button changes its meaning with repo state (Commit, Commit & push, Commit push & PR, Push, Create PR, or a hint like 'Create and checkout a ref first') and shows stage-by-stage progress ('Generating commit message...', 'Pushing to origin...', 'Creating pull request...'); each thread can run in the current checkout or its own git worktree, with a confirmation when acting on the default branch.
how: GitActionsControl.logic.resolveQuickAction(gitStatus, isBusy, isDefaultRef, hasPrimaryRemote) inspects hasBranch, hasWorkingTreeChanges, open PR, ahead/behind/diverged and default-branch delta; buildGitActionProgressStages emits the stage list per GitStackedAction (commit, commit_push, push, create_pr, commit_push_pr); requiresDefaultBranchConfirmation + DefaultBranchActionDialogCopy; resolveAutoFeatureBranchName; BranchToolbarEnvModeSelector (local|worktree) and EnvironmentSelector; settings defaultThreadEnvMode and newWorktreesStartFromOrigin; t3.json runOnWorktreeCreate runs the setup script; RPC git.runStackedAction and vcs.createWorktree/removeWorktree; worktreeCleanup.ts handles removal.
verevonRelevance: Coding-specific, but the state-derived single primary action with progress stages is a reusable pattern for multi-step agent output actions (publish, send, file).
notes: Quality 4: Excellent state-derived affordance; coding-specific.

name: Checked-in project file (t3.json) with published JSON Schema and shared scripts
what: A repository can ship a t3.json that defines team-shared scripts (name, command, icon, run on worktree creation, preview URL and auto-open), a default thread environment mode and a project icon; teammates import the scripts into their personal list and can bind each script to a shortcut.
how: contracts/t3ProjectFile.ts: T3_PROJECT_FILE_NAME 't3.json', T3_PROJECT_FILE_SCHEMA_URL https://t3.codes/schema/t3.json, annotations on the encoded side so they appear in the published JSON Schema, max 50 scripts, path max 512; server T3ProjectFileLoader (best-effort load) and ProjectSetupScriptRunner; client useT3ProjectFileScripts, ProjectScriptsControl (import file scripts, run, edit), projectScriptEditor, script.<id>.run keybinding commands (MAX_SCRIPT_ID_LENGTH 24); LAST_INVOKED_SCRIPT_BY_PROJECT_KEY remembers the primary script.

name: Serial command queue, transactional event append and idempotent command receipts
what: Every UI action is a command with an id; the server processes commands one at a time, appends events and updates projections in a single SQL transaction, publishes events afterwards, and replaying a command id returns the original outcome (accepted sequence or recorded rejection) instead of acting twice.
how: OrchestrationEngine: Queue.unbounded<CommandEnvelope>, PubSub.unbounded<OrchestrationEvent>, in-memory commandReadModel; processEnvelope reads OrchestrationCommandReceiptRepository.getByCommandId (checks the receipt's aggregate matches, returns resultSequence for accepted or the stored error for rejected), runs decider -> eventStore.append -> projectEvent -> projectionPipeline.projectEvent inside a transaction, stamps the dispatching client's origin {surface, appVersion} onto events, annotates spans (orchestration.command_id/type/aggregate), publishes to PubSub, and reconciles the read model from persisted events if dispatch fails mid-way; decider/projector/commandInvariants are pure; events carry commandId, causationEventId, correlationId, metadata{providerTurnId, providerItemId, adapterKey, requestId, ingestedAt, origin}; 43 SQLite migrations including canonicalisation of model selections (016) and shell-summary backfills (024).
verevonRelevance: This is the backbone Verevon's Model Plane sessions/runs need: idempotent commands, causal event metadata, transactional projections and replayable state, with pure decider/projector functions that port directly to Rust.
notes: Single-writer queue is simple and safe for a single-user local server; a multi-tenant cloud would shard queues per aggregate. Quality 5: Best-in-class core: idempotent receipts, causal metadata and reconcile-on-failure.

how: contracts/auth.ts: ServerAuthSessionMethod browser-session-cookie|bearer-access-token|dpop-access-token; scopes orchestration:read, orchestration:operate, terminal:operate, review:write, access:read, access:write, relay:read, relay:write with AuthStandardClientScopes and AuthAdministrativeScopes; token exchange grant type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and an environment-bootstrap token type; environment descriptor advertises policy, bootstrapMethods and sessionMethods so clients pick the UX; primary client operations fetch-session-state, exchange-bootstrap-credential, create-pairing-credential, list/revoke-pairing-link, list/revoke-client-session, revoke-other-client-sessions; server RpcAuthorization maps each RPC method to a scope; pairing token travels in the URL fragment and is stripped after exchange (stripPairingTokenFromUrl); connections settings lists devices with QR codes.

name: Global appearance sync and resilient root error view
what: Appearance preferences (contrast, glass opacity, font families and sizes, smoothing, theme) are applied to document-level CSS variables by small sync components at the root, and a crash in the root route shows a styled error view with details and a reset action instead of a blank screen.
how: routes/__root.tsx mounts ContrastAppearanceSync (applyAppearanceContrast), GlassAppearanceSync (--glass-opacity), FontAppearanceSync (applyAppearanceFontVariables), DocumentTitleSync (resolveServerBackedAppDisplayName with stage label), ThemeEditorHost above the router, ToastProvider and AnchoredToastProvider; RootRouteErrorView shows errorMessage/errorDetails with reset; RenderErrorBoundary component for panels; SlowRpcRequestToastCoordinator and ConfirmDialogHost mounted globally.
verevonRelevance: Standard but worth replicating: CSS-variable driven appearance and a branded fatal-error view.
notes: Quality 3: Standard but tidy.

name: No OS-level notifications, sounds or badge counts for finished agent work
what: Long-running threads signal completion only through in-app status pills, the unseen-completion dot and the 'Woke' indicator; no desktop notification, sound or dock badge code was found in the SPA or desktop sources.
how: Grep over SPA and desktop sources found no new Notification, Notification.requestPermission, showNotification, dock badge or Audio usage (hits were unrelated badgeCount fields); the only cross-device signal is the T3 Connect relay that can publish agent activity to mobile clients (per scout inventory, cli/connect.ts), and document.title only carries the app/stage name.
verevonRelevance: Gap to exploit: Verevon agents that run for minutes or hours need push/email/desktop notifications with per-thread controls; T3 relies on staying in the app. Baseline check: Verevon already ships a 'Notify me when done' run watcher via notification-core, so this is T3's gap, not a Verevon one.
notes: Absence claim; confidence medium because only keyword searches were used. Quality 2: Absence of a basic feature for long-running work.

name: Model default resolution: sticky last choice, per-project default, provider default
what: A new thread starts with the model you used last (remembered per provider instance together with its effort/option choices), falls back to the project's default model, then to the provider's default; project settings expose that default and the default workspace mode.
how: composerDraftStore keeps stickyModelSelectionByProvider (Partial<Record<ProviderInstanceId, ModelSelection>>) and stickyActiveProvider with migration code from v2 dual fields to the consolidated shape; setStickyComposerModelSelection is called in ChatView.onProviderModelSelect; ChatComposer.selectedInstanceId resolves composerDraft.activeProvider, then the thread's session or model selection, then activeProject.defaultModelSelection, then the first compatible enabled instance; ProjectSettingsPanel 'New threads' section sets Model ('Applies to every checkout in this group') and Workspace (overrides t3.json and the global default); DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_PROVIDER and getDefaultServerModel provide the last fallback.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same layered default (last used, space default, org default) with org policy able to override; keeping per-provider remembered options avoids resetting reasoning effort on every switch.
notes: Quality 4: Layered and sticky defaults handled with migrations.

name: Per-project settings page (name, icon, defaults, checkout, grouping, validation)
what: Each project group has a settings page for its shared name, icon (file or t3.json), default model for new threads, default workspace mode (local or worktree), which checkout to inspect, grouping behaviour and a danger zone; an invalid t3.json produces an explicit explanation instead of silently ignoring it.
how: routes/projects.$projectKey.tsx renders ProjectSettingsPanel (47KB) with 'Switch project' selector, Project (Name, Project icon via ProjectFaviconPickerDialog), New threads (Model, Workspace), Checkout (path copy, remove checkout 'Files on disk are not touched'), Project grouping, and a warning 'A t3.json exists in this checkout but fails to parse, so every action and icon it declares is ignored.'; settings use the same SettingsSection/SettingResetButton primitives as global settings.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon space settings; the explicit invalid-config message is a good habit for any file-based configuration.
notes: Quality 4: Clear and complete with explicit invalid-config messaging.

name: Lifecycle banners above the composer: background work with Stop, snoozed/settled/woke states
what: When an agent keeps working after its turn ends, a banner says '3 agents working' (or 'Monitoring') with a Stop button; opening a snoozed or settled thread shows 'This thread is snoozed/settled - sending a message moves it back to Active' with a Wake now / Un-settle action, and a woken thread says why it woke.
how: ChatView builds ComposerBannerStackItems: backgroundLivenessBannerItem (pulsing dot via animate-status-pulse, title from agentPanelModel.liveCount or 'Monitoring', Stop -> handleStopBackgroundWork -> interruptThreadTurn with error surfaced in the thread error banner), wokeThreadBannerItem ('This thread woke from snooze', dismissal clears the Woke indicator), parkedThreadBannerItem (info variant, AlarmClockIcon/CheckCircle2Icon, wake/unsettle handlers with 'Waking...' states), resumeCompactionBannerItem, and systemComposerBannerItems ordered so urgent error/warning banners come first and the informational parked-thread banner never covers another; backgroundLiveness comes from the thread shell.
verevonRelevance: Persistent, in-context status with a stop control for background agent work is essential for Verevon agent pages; state-explaining banners avoid the 'why is this thread hidden' confusion.
notes: Quality 4: Context-rich status with actions; excellent explanation of hidden states.

name: Screen recordings and screenshots of the agent's browser session
what: Either the user or the agent can record the in-app browser tab to a video file (MP4 H.264 when supported, otherwise WebM) and capture screenshots; artifacts can be copied or revealed in the file manager, giving a shareable proof of what the agent did.
how: browser/browserRecording.ts records a canvas stream at 12 fps (canvas.captureStream(12)) with MediaRecorder at 4 Mbps, choosing among video/mp4;codecs=avc1.42E01E, video/webm;codecs=vp9, video/webm; typed errors BrowserRecordingUnavailableError, BrowserRecordingConflictError (one active recording at a time), BrowserRecordingCanvasUnavailableError; frames arrive from the desktop webview via desktop:preview-recording-start/-frame/-stop/-save; desktop:preview-capture-screenshot, -copy-artifact, -reveal-artifact; agents use MCP tools preview_recording_start/preview_recording_stop and preview_snapshot.
verevonRelevance: Recording and screenshots of computer-use sessions are a strong audit and sharing feature for Verevon's browser-control agents (store as run artifacts in the Data plane).
notes: Desktop-only; relies on Chromium webview frames. Quality 4: Working recording pipeline; limited to the desktop webview.

name: Web search surfaced only as grouped tool activity (no sources or citations UI)
what: When a backend model searches the web, T3 shows it as a 'Searched the web N times' item inside the tool group; there are no source cards, citation markers, link previews or research report views.
how: CanonicalItemType includes web_search and image_view as tool lifecycle types; MessagesTimeline.logic.toolGroupAction classifies entries (read, edit, command, code-search, search, other) and toolGroupActionLabel prints 'Searched the web N time(s)'; a heuristic reclassifies web_search items whose title contains grep as 'Searched code'; summaries are provider-neutral text built by summarizeToolGroup ('Read 4 files, ran 2 commands and searched the web 1 time'); no citation, source or footnote rendering found in ChatMarkdown (only generic external-link favicons and a context menu).
verevonRelevance: Clear gap and opportunity: Verevon chat should render sources and citations as first-class UI (source cards, inline markers, per-claim grounding) that T3 lacks.
notes: Absence-of-feature record; the verdict rests on code search over the recovered SPA tree. Quality 2: Minimal: no sources or citations.

name: Collaborative browser tool surface: Playwright locators, semantic snapshots, MCP safety annotations
what: The agent drives the same browser tab the user sees through 14 tools; it is told to snapshot first, then act with Playwright-style locators (role=button[name='Send'], text=Continue) rather than raw coordinates, and each tool declares whether it is read-only, idempotent or destructive.
how: mcp/toolkits/preview/tools.ts builds Effect AI Tool definitions with MCP annotations (OpenWorld on all; Destructive true for click, type, press and evaluate; Destructive false for open, navigate, resize, set_appearance, scroll and recording start/stop; Readonly+Idempotent for status, snapshot and wait_for; PreviewToolkit and PreviewStandardToolkit variants); contracts/previewAutomation.ts input schemas require exactly one of locator, selector (legacy CSS) or x/y, and validate mutual exclusion with error messages; preview_snapshot returns page state, semantic elements, diagnostics and action history; preview_navigate accepts a URL or {target:{kind:'environment-port',port:5173}} for dev servers; preview_resize supports fill, freeform or device presets with orientation; preview_set_appearance emulates prefers-color-scheme; desktop PlaywrightInjectedRuntime extracts Playwright's injected-script source from the installed playwright-core bundle by string markers and evaluates it (vm, 1 s timeout) so locator strings resolve inside the webview without a full Playwright session.
verevonRelevance: A concrete, small computer-use tool vocabulary with semantic targeting and safety annotations to compare against Quarry's browser grants; destructive/readonly annotations map to Verevon's approval policy per tool. Baseline check: Verevon lets the model propose browser actions that Quarry executes or rejects; T3's locator-first vocabulary and destructive/readonly annotations map onto that proposal contract.
notes: Extracting Playwright internals by string markers is brittle across Playwright upgrades (PLAYWRIGHT_SOURCE_MARKER, TERMINATOR constants). Quality 4: Thoughtful tool vocabulary and annotations; Playwright internals extraction is brittle.

name: Type-anywhere-to-focus composer and editing niceties (surround selection, IME safety)
what: Typing a printable key while nothing else owns focus sends the keystroke to the composer; selecting text and typing a bracket or quote wraps the selection; IME composition, dead keys and open menus are respected.
how: ChatView.shouldTypeToFocusComposer ignores defaultPrevented, isComposing, meta/ctrl/alt, non-printable keys, events whose composed path hits an editable or interactive selector, any open floating layer (dialog, menu, select, popover, combobox, autocomplete) and keys claimed by the right-panel launcher (data-surface-launcher-keys); ComposerSurroundSelectionPlugin (SURROUND_SYMBOLS_MAP, pending selection refs, dead-key handling) wraps selections through Lexical updates; ComposerHomeEndKeyPlugin and arrow plugins treat inline chips as single characters; sidebar toggle shortcut is captured before the editor consumes Mod+B.
verevonRelevance: A chat-first product benefits from 'just start typing' focus management; the guard list (editable, interactive, floating layers, IME) is the part that usually goes wrong.
notes: Quality 4: Carefully guarded keyboard behaviour.

name: Fast file picker and project content search backed by a native index
what: Cmd+P opens a fuzzy file picker (up to 200 results, matched characters highlighted) and Cmd+Shift+F searches file contents with case-sensitive and whole-word toggles, both feeding mentions, the file panel or the editor.
how: ProjectFilePicker with PROJECT_FILE_PICKER_RESULT_LIMIT 200 and findMatchIndices for ordered-subsequence highlighting of name and path; RPC projects.searchEntries and projects.searchContents (ProjectSearchContentsInput/Result in contracts/project.ts); server WorkspaceSearchIndex on the @ff-labs/fff native library (libfff_c) with packages/shared/searchRanking for scoring; ProjectContentSearchDialog with caseSensitive and wholeWord toggles and HighlightedSearchLine; keybindings filePicker.toggle (mod+p) and projectSearch.toggle (mod+shift+f); search overlays share the palette reducer so they never stack.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's equivalent is 'go to document/record' and 'search within sources'; the instant fuzzy-with-highlight picker is a good UX template over the Data plane.
notes: Native index (fff) is a non-portable dependency. Quality 4: Fast and polished; native index dependency.

name: Purposeful micro-animations with reduced-motion fallbacks
what: Small, meaningful motion: a pulsing dot for working states, a shimmering 'focus' sweep on the currently running tool row, a ping on the agent cursor, a counter animation when the prompt stash grows, a progress line while a preview loads, and a rainbow shimmer on the composer in ultrathink mode; most are disabled under reduced motion.
how: Built CSS keyframes: status-pulse, status-ping, live-activity-focus (+counter), ghost-pulse (skeleton for PR rows), prompt-stash-count-enter (180 ms), preview-loading-progress, provider-update-pill-countdown, settings-search-target-pulse, t3-mobile-composer-new/old and t3-mobile-draft-headline-exit (View Transitions), ultrathink-chroma-shift and ultrathink-rainbow; Tailwind classes motion-reduce:animate-none, motion-reduce:transition-none, motion-reduce:transform-none; AnimatedHeight and @formkit/auto-animate for expanding sections; ContextWindowMeter ring transitions 500 ms ease-out with motion-reduce:transition-none.
verevonRelevance: Motion budget reference for Verevon: status feedback and shimmer on the live tool row, always paired with a reduced-motion fallback.
notes: Reduced-motion coverage is partial (some animations only), see accessibility record. Quality 4: Tasteful and mostly motion-safe.

name: Battery-aware background activity profiles
what: Polling work (git fetch, provider health checks, host power monitoring) follows a selectable profile - Performance, Balanced, Battery saver or Custom - and pauses when the host is locked, on battery or low power, or when no client has been connected for 45 seconds.
how: contracts BackgroundActivityProfile balanced|performance|battery-saver (+custom selection) with overrides {automaticGitFetchInterval, providerHealthRefreshInterval, hostPowerMonitorActiveInterval, hostPowerMonitorIdleInterval, idleClientTtl, pauseWhenHostLocked, pauseWhenHostLowPower, pauseWhenClientLowPower, pauseWhenOnBattery}; shared/backgroundActivitySettings.ts PRESET_SETTINGS (performance: git fetch 15 s, provider health 1 min; balanced: 30 s and 5 min; battery-saver: git fetch off, 15 min health, pause on battery); clients report activity via lib/backgroundActivityReporter.ts and RPC server.reportHostPowerState/getBackgroundPolicy; server BackgroundPolicy and HostPowerMonitor; settings schemaVersion 1 with legacy flat fields kept for old clients.
verevonRelevance: Mostly a local-runtime concern, but the profile-with-overrides pattern and client-activity-driven pausing could govern Verevon background refreshes (connectors, indexing previews) for mobile and battery use.
notes: Server file cited from scout inventory; SPA and shared files verified. Quality 4: Unusually thoughtful local-runtime tuning.

name: Steer a running agent: send while running continues the same turn
what: While the agent is working, the user can keep typing and send; the message is queued into the live agent loop and the work continues as the same turn (no synthetic boundary), with a red Stop button always available beside Send; on mobile Enter still inserts a newline so Stop and Send are explicit buttons.
how: ClaudeAdapter.sendTurn treats a send during a real (non-synthetic) turn as a steer: steeringTurnState reuses the turn id and queues the message into the SDK agent loop, while stale synthetic turns (opened by background agent output between prompts) are auto-closed first; ProviderRuntimeIngestion and ProjectionPipeline contain comments about steering opening new turns on some providers (opencode); client ChatView.logic.hasServerAcknowledgedLocalDispatch treats a newly projected user message as the server acknowledgment while phase is 'running' so the composer does not stay in 'Sending'; ComposerPrimaryActions renders the Stop generation button (rounded, destructive colour, size changes when showSendWhileRunning && hasSendableContent) plus the send button; MessagesTimeline derives fold boundaries so a turn cut short by a steer stays coherent.
verevonRelevance: Baseline check: Verevon already ships mid-run messages queued into the live run (pending/delivered/refused states); T3's refinement is the same-turn semantics and explicit acknowledgement via projected messages.
notes: Steer semantics differ per provider; the Claude adapter is the documented one. Quality 4: Clear same-turn semantics; provider-dependent.

name: Cache-first rendering from IndexedDB snapshots with visible sync state
what: Opening the app or a thread paints immediately from locally cached snapshots (projects, thread shells, thread details, server config, git refs) while the live connection catches up; the user sees 'Loading messages...' or 'Syncing messages...' and a colour-coded connection dot instead of a blank screen.
how: web connection/storage.ts opens IndexedDB 't3code:connection-runtime' (version 4) with stores catalog, shell, thread, server-config, vcs-refs and Schema-validated documents (SHELL_SNAPSHOT_CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION 1, ConnectionCatalogDocument schemaVersion 1 holding targets, profiles, credentials, remoteDpopTokens); client-runtime platform/persistence defines EnvironmentCacheStore operations load/save/remove for shell, thread, server-config and vcs-refs plus clear-environment; EnvironmentThreadStatus empty|cached|synchronizing|live|deleted drives resolveThreadSyncPhase (loading when no detail, syncing when cached detail exists) and ThreadSyncStatusPill (role=status); connectionPhaseDotClassName maps connected/connecting/reconnecting/error to success/warning/destructive dots with a ping halo for transitional phases; snapshots are fetched over HTTP then resumed by sequence (see sync record).
verevonRelevance: Instant, offline-tolerant first paint is a clear UX win for Verevon; a per-environment IndexedDB cache with versioned schemas plus an honest 'syncing' state avoids spinners and stale surprises.
notes: Credentials and DPoP tokens live in the same catalog document store (IndexedDB), which is a security trade-off worth reviewing before copying. Quality 4: Good first-paint design; credentials share the same store.

name: Workflow runs shown as phases with member agents and an inspectable script
what: Multi-agent workflow runs appear as a collapsible group with a phase rail, phase sections that open themselves when they start running and stay put when they settle, a 'X/Y settled' counter, token totals, and a '{} script' toggle that shows the workflow's source read-only.
how: RuntimeSubagent.kind subagent|workflow|workflow_agent with phaseIndex/phaseTitle, attempt, workflowName, phases[], parentAgentId, agentIndex, runHandles {runId, scriptPath, transcriptDir, sessionUrl}, usage {totalTokens, inputTokens, cachedInputTokens, outputTokens, reasoningOutputTokens, toolUses, durationMs}, recentActivity ring and lastToolName; deriveAgentPanelModel groups into AgentPanelWorkflowGroup {workflow, phases[{state pending|running|done, activeCount, settledCount, members}], unphasedMembers} plus AgentPanelModel counters (runningCount, waitingCount, idleCount, settledCount, totalTokens, liveCount); AgentsPanel PhaseSection (auto-open on running, manual toggles stick), CollapsedWorkflowSection summary line, WorkflowScriptView loads contents through RPC orchestration.getWorkflowScript (server limits reads to the Claude projects folder by realpath; result may be truncated with a notice).
verevonRelevance: If Verevon agent pages orchestrate multi-step workflows, a phase-grouped roster with live counters and an inspectable plan/script is a ready-made presentation model; the realpath-contained read is the right security pattern for showing generated scripts.
notes: Workflow scripts are provider-native (Claude); the viewer is read-only. Quality 4: Well-considered live-state rules; provider-native scripts only.
